q.o: Gaudete, quia evasistis fluctuantis mundi multimoda pericula et naufragia. Gaudete, quia quietam et tutam stationem portus secretioris obtinuistis, ad quem cum multi venire desiderent, multi quoque non nullo conatu contendant, non perveniunt tamen.

q.t: As for me, brothers, know that after God my one desire is to come to you and to see you. And when I am able, I will fulfil it in deed, with God's help.
q.l: Letter from Calabria to his brothers at the Grande Chartreuse, closing words, n. 682 (Acta Sanctorum Oct. III, p. 615)
q.o: De me, Fratres, scitote, quoniam mihi unicum post Deum est desiderium veniendi ad vos, et videndi vos. Et quando potero, opere adimplebo, Deo adjuvante.

q.t: He descended into hell to set free his captives there; he descended for our redemption, and he rose again. He ascended into heaven, and from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.
q.l: Profession of faith made to his brethren as death approached, as recorded by his disciples, n. 727 (Acta Sanctorum Oct. III, p. 687)
q.o: Descendit ad inferos, ut captivos suos inde liberaret, descendit propter redemptionem nostram , et resurrexit. Ascendit ad caelos, inde venturus est judicare vivos et mortuos.

q.t: Yet since it has pleased the divine will to raise Our lowliness to such fullness of power, We lift up Our heart in him who strengtheneth Us; and, setting Our hand to the work in reliance on the power of God, We declare that in carrying out Our pontificate We have this one aim: to re-establish all things in Christ, so that Christ may be all, and in all.
q.w: E supremi (encyclical on the restoration of all things in Christ)
q.l: Encyclical of 4 October 1903; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 129-139
q.o: Attamen, quoniam numini divino placuit humilitatem Nostram ad hanc amplitudinem potestatis provehere; erigimus animum in eo qui Nos confortat, Deique virtute freti manum operi admoventes, in gerendo pontificatu hoc unum declaramus propositum esse Nobis instaurare omnia in Christo, ut videlicet sit omnia et in omnibus Christus.

q.t: The longing for peace surely touches every heart, and there is no one who does not call for it earnestly. Yet to seek peace while rejecting God is absurd: for where God is absent, justice is banished, and once justice is taken away, it is vain to hope for peace. The work of justice shall be peace.
q.w: E supremi (encyclical on the restoration of all things in Christ)
q.l: Encyclical of 4 October 1903; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 129-139
q.o: Cupiditas pacis omnium, profecto pectora attingit, eamque nemo est qui non invocet vehementer. Pax tamen, reiecto Numine, absurde quaeritur: unde namque abest Deus, iustitia exsulat; sublataque iustitia, frustra in spem pacis venitur. Opus iustitiae pax.

q.t: How great indeed was the gentleness of that divine Master! What sweetness, what compassion for all who were in distress! Isaiah painted his heart exactly in these words: "I will put my spirit upon him; he shall not contend, nor cry out; the bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not extinguish."
q.w: E supremi (encyclical on the restoration of all things in Christ)
q.l: Encyclical of 4 October 1903; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 129-139
q.o: Quanta enimvero in divino illo magistro mansuetudo ! quae suavitas, quae in aerumnosos quoslibet miseratio! Cor eius plane pinxit Isaias iis verbis: Ponam spiritum meum super eum; non contendet neque clamabit; arundinem quassatam non confringet et linum fumigans non extinguet.

q.t: Why should we not hope that the flame of Christian charity will drive the darkness from souls and bring with it the light and the peace of God? The fruit of our labour may at times be slow in coming; but charity never wearies of waiting, for it remembers that God has promised his rewards not to the fruits of our labours but to our will.
q.w: E supremi (encyclical on the restoration of all things in Christ)
q.l: Encyclical of 4 October 1903; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 129-139
q.o: Quidni speremus christianae caritatis flammam ab animis caliginem dispulsuram atque allaturam simul Dei lumen et pacem? Tardabitur quandoque forsitan laboris nostri fructus: sed caritas sustentatione nunquam defatigatur, memor non esse praemia a Deo proposita laborum fructibus sed voluntati.

q.t: For who does not know that there is no surer or easier way than through Mary to unite all men with Christ, and through him to obtain the perfect adoption of sons, that we may be holy and unspotted in the sight of God?
q.w: Ad diem illum (encyclical on the Immaculate Conception)
q.l: Encyclical of 2 February 1904; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 449-462
q.o: Nam cui exploratum non sit nullum, praeterquam per Mariam, esse certius et expeditius iter ad universos cum Christo iungendos, perque illum perfectam filiorum adoptionem assequendam ut simus sancti et immaculati in conspectu Dei ?

q.t: Mary not only kept, pondering them in her heart, the things that took place at Bethlehem and in the temple of the Lord at Jerusalem; but, sharing in the counsels and hidden purposes of Christ, she must be said to have lived the very life of her Son. No one, therefore, has known Christ as deeply as she; no one is a fitter guide and teacher for coming to know Christ.
q.w: Ad diem illum (encyclical on the Immaculate Conception)
q.l: Encyclical of 2 February 1904; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 449-462
q.o: Quae quidem non ea modo conservabat conferens in corde suo quae Bethlehem acta, quaeve Hierosolymis in templo Domini; sed Christi consiliorum particeps occultarumque voluntatum, vitam ipsam Filii vixisse dicenda est. Nemo itaque penitus ut illa Christum novit; nemo illa aptior dux et magister ad Christum noscendum.

q.t: Indeed, no honour is more desired by Mary, none more pleasing to her, than that we should rightly know and love Jesus. Let there be, then, celebrations of the faithful in the churches, festive decorations, rejoicing in the cities: all these things are of no small help in fostering piety. Yet unless the will of the heart is joined to them, we shall have mere forms that offer only the appearance of religion.
q.w: Ad diem illum (encyclical on the Immaculate Conception)
q.l: Encyclical of 2 February 1904; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 449-462
q.o: Nullus equidem honor Mariae optabilior, nullus iucundior quam ut noscamus rite et amemus Iesum. Sint igitur fidelium celebritates in templis, sint festi apparatus, sint laetitiae civitatum; quae res omnes non mediocres usus afferunt ad pietatem fovendam. Verumtamen nisi his voluntas animi accedat, formas habebimus, quae speciem tantum offerant relligionis.

q.t: John, then, saw the most holy Mother of God already enjoying eternal bliss, and yet labouring in a mysterious childbirth. What birth? Ours, surely: for we, still held in exile, have yet to be brought forth into the perfect love of God and everlasting happiness. Her travail shows the zeal and love with which the Virgin, from her heavenly throne, keeps watch and strives by unceasing prayer that the number of the elect may be filled up.
q.w: Ad diem illum (encyclical on the Immaculate Conception)
q.l: Encyclical of 2 February 1904; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 449-462
q.o: Vidit igitur Ioannes sanctissimam Dei Matrem aeterna iam beatitate fruentem, et tamen ex arcano quodam partu laborantem. Quonam autem partu? Nostrum plane, qui exilio adhuc detenti, ad perfectam Dei caritatem sempiternamque felicitatem gignendi adhuc sumus. Parientis vero labor studium atque amorem indicat, quo Virgo, in caelesti sede, vigilat assiduaque prece contendit ut electorum numerus expleatur.

q.t: For Christian wisdom makes known to us God and what we call his infinite perfections far more clearly than the powers of nature can search them out. And what follows? It bids us also to honour that supreme God with the duty of faith, which belongs to the mind; of hope, which belongs to the will; and of charity, which belongs to the heart; and so it gives the whole man over to that supreme Author and Ruler.
q.w: Acerbo nimis (encyclical on teaching Christian doctrine)
q.l: Encyclical of 15 April 1905; Acta Sanctae Sedis 37 (1904-05), 613-625
q.o: Deum namque eiusque infinitas quas perfectiones nominamus, longe exploratius, quam naturae vires scrutentur, christiana nobis sapientia manifestat. Quid porro? Iubet haec simul summum ipsum Deum officio fidei nos revereri, quae mentis est; spei quae voluntatis; caritatis quae cordis: sicque totum hominem supremo illi Auctori ac Moderatori mancipat.

q.t: From birth, man has the power of understanding; yet it needs a mother's word to rouse it, as it were, so that it may pass, as they say, into act. It is no different with the Christian: born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he brings with him the faith conceived in him; yet he needs the teaching of the Church, so that this faith may be nourished, may grow, and may bear fruit.
q.w: Acerbo nimis (encyclical on teaching Christian doctrine)
q.l: Encyclical of 15 April 1905; Acta Sanctae Sedis 37 (1904-05), 613-625
q.o: Est et in homine, ab exortu, intelligendi vis: ea tamen materno indiget verbo, quo quasi excitata in actum, ut aiunt, exeat. Haud aliter christiano homini accidit, qui, renascens ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, conceptam secum affert fidem; eget tamen Ecclesiae institutione, ut ea ali augerique possit fructumque ferre.

q.t: Since, as everyone knows, holiness of life is the fruit of our will only in so far as that will is strengthened by God with the help of grace, God himself has amply provided that, if we wish, we need never at any time be without the gift of grace; and this we obtain above all by devotion to prayer. Indeed, prayer and holiness are so necessarily bound together that the one can by no means exist without the other.
q.w: Haerent animo (exhortation to the Catholic clergy)
q.l: Exhortation of 4 August 1908; Acta Sanctae Sedis 41 (1908), 555-577
q.o: Quoniam vero, ut nemo unus ignorat, vitae sanctitas eatenus fructus est voluntatis nostrae, quoad haec gratiae subsidio roboretur a Deo, abunde nobis Deus ipse providit, ne gratiae munere, si velimus, ullo tempore careamus; idque in primis assequimur studio precandi. — Sane precationem inter et sanctimoniam is necessario intercedit usus, ut altera esse sine altera nullo modo possit.

q.t: What of the fact that even devout hearts are so easily soiled by the dust of the world? It is plain, then, how great and how pressing is the need to return each day to the contemplation of eternal things, so that mind and will, their strength renewed again and again, may be made firm against temptations.
q.w: Haerent animo (exhortation to the Catholic clergy)
q.l: Exhortation of 4 August 1908; Acta Sanctae Sedis 41 (1908), 555-577
q.o: Quid, quod tam est proclive, de mundano pulvere etiam religiosa corda sordescere? Apparet igitur quae et quanta urgeat necessitas ad aeternorum contemplationem quotidie redeundi, ut adversus illecebras mens et voluntas, renovato subinde robore, obfirmentur.

q.t: There is, in truth, one thing that unites man with God, one thing that makes him pleasing to God and a not unworthy minister of his mercy: holiness of life and conduct. If a priest lacks this, which is in the end the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ, he lacks everything.
q.w: Haerent animo (exhortation to the Catholic clergy)
q.l: Exhortation of 4 August 1908; Acta Sanctae Sedis 41 (1908), 555-577
q.o: Unum nimirum est quod hominem cum Deo coniungat, unum quod gratum efficiat, atque non indignum eius misericordiae administrum vitae morumque, sanctimonia. Haec, quae demum est supereminens Iesu Christi scientia, sacerdoti si desit, desunt ei omnia.

q.t: But above all, as his ministers in that most excellent Sacrifice which, by its unfailing power, is renewed for the life of the world, we must have the same disposition of soul with which he offered himself on the altar of the cross as a spotless victim to God. For if of old, in a mere type and figure, such holiness was required of priests, what is required of us, when the victim is Christ?
q.w: Haerent animo (exhortation to the Catholic clergy)
q.l: Exhortation of 4 August 1908; Acta Sanctae Sedis 41 (1908), 555-577
q.o: At maxime ut ministri eius in praecellentissimo sacrificio, quod perenni virtute pro mundi vita innovatur, debemus ea animi conformatione uti, qua ille ad aram crucis seipsum obtulit hostiam immaculatam Deo. Nam si olim, in specie solummodo ac figura, tanta a sacerdotibus postulabatur sanctitas; ecquid a nobis, quum victima est Christus?

q.t: For since it is Our most ardent desire that the true Christian spirit should flourish again in every way and be maintained in all the faithful, it is necessary before all else to provide for the holiness and dignity of the temple, where the faithful gather precisely to draw that spirit from its first and indispensable source, which is active participation in the most holy mysteries and in the public and solemn prayer of the Church.
q.w: Tra le sollecitudini (motu proprio on sacred music)
q.l: Motu proprio of 22 November 1903; Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), 329-339
q.o: Essendo, infatti, Nostro vivissimo desiderio che il vero spirito cristiano rifiorisca per ogni modo e si mantenga nei fedeli tutti, è necessario provvedere prima di ogni altra cosa alla santità e dignità del tempio, dove appunto i fedeli si radunano per attingere tale spirito dalla sua prima ed indispensabile fonte, che è la partecipazione attiva ai sacrosanti misteri e alla preghiera pubblica e solenne della Chiesa.

q.t: As we must continue and fulfil in ourselves the life, virtues and actions of Jesus on earth, so too we must continue and fulfil in ourselves the states and mysteries of Jesus, and often pray this same Jesus to consummate and fulfil them in us and in his whole Church. For it is a truth worthy of being noted and pondered more than once, that the mysteries of Jesus are not yet in their full perfection and fulfilment.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part III, §4 'That we are obliged to have a special devotion to all the states and mysteries of the life of Jesus'
q.o: comme nous devons continuer et accomplir en nous la vie, les vertus et actions de Jésus sur la terre, aussi nous devons continuer et accomplir en nous les états et mystères de Jésus, et prier souvent ce même Jésus qu'il les consomme et accomplisse en nous et en toute son Église. Car c'est une vérité digne d'être remarquée et considérée plus d'une fois, que les mystères de Jésus ne sont pas encore dans leur entière perfection et accomplissement.

q.t: The holy exercise of prayer must be placed among the chief foundations of Christian life and holiness, because the whole life of Jesus Christ was nothing but a perpetual prayer, which we must continue and express in our own life.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part II, §11 'On the fourth foundation of the Christian life and holiness, which is prayer'
q.o: Le saint exercice de l'oraison doit être mis au rang des principaux fondements de la vie et sainteté chrétienne, parce que toute la vie de Jésus-Christ n'a été qu'une perpétuelle oraison, laquelle nous devons continuer et exprimer en notre vie

q.t: It is this virtue, joined with sacred love, that makes saints, and great saints. For the true measure of holiness is humility.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part II, §25 'On the dignity, necessity and importance of Christian humility'; Œuvres complètes, t. I (1905), p. 214
q.o: C'est cette vertu, jointe avec l'amour sacré, qui fait les saints et les grands saints. Car la vraie mesure de la sainteté, c'est l'humilité.

q.t: If we look at the Church of God in the light of faith, we shall see that, having Jesus Christ for her head and the Holy Spirit for her guide, it is impossible that she should in anything stray from the truth or wander into falsehood.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part II, §4 'On the first foundation of the Christian life and holiness, which is faith'
q.o: Si nous regardons l'Église de Dieu en la lumière de la foi, nous verrons qu'ayant Jésus-Christ pour son chef et le Saint-Esprit pour son conducteur, il est impossible qu'elle puisse en aucune chose s'éloigner de la vérité, ni s'égarer dans le mensonge

q.t: This is how we must look at all things: not in the vanity of our senses, nor with the eyes of flesh and blood, nor with the short and deceptive sight of human reason and knowledge, but in the truth of God and with the eyes of Jesus Christ.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part II, §4 'On the first foundation of the Christian life and holiness, which is faith'
q.o: C'est ainsi qu'il nous faut regarder toutes choses, non pas en la vanité de nos sens, ni avec les yeux de la chair et du sang, ni avec la courte et trompeuse vue de la raison et de la science humaine, mais en la vérité de Dieu et avec les yeux de Jésus-Christ

q.t: As our Lord Jesus Christ comes to us in the most holy Eucharist with very great humility, which makes him stoop even to taking the form and appearance of bread to give himself to us, and with a most ardent love, which moves him to give us in this sacrament all he has that is greatest, dearest and most precious: so we must approach him and receive him in this same sacrament with very deep humility and very great love.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part I, 'For Holy Communion' (introduction to §18); Œuvres complètes, t. I (1905), p. 137
q.o: Comme Notre-Seigneur Jésus-Christ vient à nous par la très sainte Eucharistie, avec une très grande humilité, qui le fait [s'] abaisser jusqu'à prendre la forme et l'apparence de pain, pour se donner à nous ; et avec un amour très ardent qui le porte à nous donner, dans ce sacrement, tout ce qu'il a de plus grand, de plus cher et de plus précieux : aussi nous devons nous approcher de lui et le recevoir en ce même sacrement, avec une très profonde humilité et un très grand amour.

q.t: We shall look upon this day as if it were the last of our days, and we shall try to spend it with as much care and devotion as if there remained to us only this day in which to love God.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part VII, exercise for dying in a Christian manner, Seventh Day, §26 'On the agony and the moment of death'
q.o: Nous regarderons ce jour comme si c'était le dernier de nos jours, et nous tâcherons de l'employer avec autant de soin et de dévotion comme s'il ne nous restait plus que ce jour pour aimer Dieu.

q.t: Truly, if we celebrate the memory of the day of our birth into the life of grace through holy Baptism, much more must we celebrate the day and the feast of our entrance into heaven and of our birth into the life of glory.
q.w: The Life and Kingdom of Jesus in Christian Souls
q.l: Part VII, exercise for dying in a Christian manner, Tenth Day, §29 'On the entrance of our souls into heaven and into immortal life'
q.o: Certes si nous célébrons la mémoire du jour de notre naissance dans la vie de grâce par le saint Baptême, beaucoup davantage devons-nous célébrer le jour et la fête de notre entrée dans le ciel et de notre naissance dans la vie de gloire.

q.t: So it is that the Heart of Jesus loves us not only in heaven or in some other place; but it loves us in heaven and on earth, it loves us in the sun, in the stars and in all created things. It loves us in all the hearts of all the dwellers in heaven, and in the hearts of all the people on earth who have any charity for us.
q.w: The Admirable Heart of the Most Holy Mother of God
q.l: Book XII, 'Eight other meditations on the divine Heart of Jesus', 4th meditation 'That the Heart of Jesus loves us…
q.o: De sorte que le Cœur de Jésus ne nous aime pas seulement dans le ciel ou en quelque autre lieu ; mais il nous aime dans le ciel et dans la terre, il nous aime dans le soleil, dans les étoiles et dans toutes les choses créées. Il nous aime dans tous les cœurs de tous les habitants du ciel, et dans les cœurs de toutes les personnes qui ont quelque charité pour nous en la terre

q.t: Heart of Jesus and Mary, priceless treasure of all good things, be my only treasure, my refuge and my safeguard! It is to you that I will have recourse in all my needs and necessities; for even if all the hearts of all men should deceive and abandon me, I have very great confidence that the most good and most faithful Heart of my lovable Jesus and of his most sweet Mother will never deceive me nor abandon me.
q.w: The Admirable Heart of the Most Holy Mother of God
q.l: Book XII, ch. 20 'Forty flames or aspirations of love toward the lovable Heart of Jesus', no. 39
q.o: Cœur de Jésus et de Marie, trésor inestimable de toutes sortes de biens, soyez mon unique trésor, mon refuge et ma sauvegarde ! C'est à vous que je veux avoir recours en tous mes besoins et nécessités ; car quand tous les cœurs de tous les hommes me tromperaient et m'abandonneraient, j'ai une très grande confiance que le très bon et très fidèle Cœur de mon aimable Jésus et de sa très douce Mère ne me tromperont point et ne m'abandonneront jamais.

q.t: Jesus, only Son of God, who willed to be the only Son of Mary and to number us among her children and your brothers, make us sharers, we pray you, in the love you bear her, and also in the love she bears you, so that we may love Jesus with the Heart of Mary, and love Mary with the Heart of Jesus.
q.w: The Admirable Heart of the Most Holy Mother of God
q.l: Book X, ch. 14 (closing prayer of Book X); Œuvres complètes, t. VIII (1908), p. 105
q.o: Jésus, Fils unique de Dieu, qui avez voulu être le Fils unique de Marie et nous mettre au rang de ses enfants et de vos frères, faites-nous participants, s'il vous plaît, de l'amour que vous lui portez, comme aussi de l'amour qu'elle vous porte, afin que nous aimions Jésus avec le Cœur de Marie, et que nous aimions Marie avec le Cœur de Jésus

q.t: It is a Heart that is always watching over us and over the smallest things that concern us. It is a Heart so full of kindness, gentleness, mercy and generosity that no one who has called upon this Mother of goodness with humility and confidence has ever gone away from her presence without consolation.
q.w: The Admirable Heart of the Most Holy Mother of God
q.l: Book XI, ch. 2 'Twelve means of honouring the most holy Heart of the Blessed Virgin', eleventh means
q.o: C'est un Cœur qui veille toujours sur nous et sur les plus petites choses qui nous touchent. C'est un Cœur si plein de bénignité, de douceur, de miséricorde et de libéralité, que jamais aucun de ceux qui ont invoqué cette Mère de bonté avec humilité et confiance, ne s'en est retourné de devant sa face sans consolation.

q.t: The Eucharist is the memorial of all the mysteries; it renews their love and their grace. You must, like Mary, respond to this grace by reviving all the actions of our Lord, by adoring all his states, and by uniting yourselves to them.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: First Day, 'Mary, Mother of the adorers of the Eucharist', meditation III; 7th ed. (1909), pp. 13-14
q.o: L'Eucharistie est le mémorial de tous les mystères, elle en renouvelle l'amour et la grâce. Il vous faut, comme Marie, correspondre à cette grâce en ravivant toutes les actions de Notre-Seigneur, en adorant tous ses états, et en vous y unissant.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: One is powerful with God only through purity, only through holiness; God does great things only through pure souls; he hears only innocent or purified voices.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Third Day, 'The dowry of Mary Immaculate', meditation III; 7th ed. (1909), p. 22
q.o: On n'est puissant auprès de Dieu que par la pureté, que par la sainteté ; Dieu ne fait de grandes choses que par les âmes pures; il n'exauce que les voix innocentes ou purifiées.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: Today people seek only to be seen; they want to arrive and enjoy at once; they do not know how to wait; they force the plant: at first it yields a great deal, but it exhausts itself and dies after a short time. Love, then, the simple and hidden life, the modest duties of your station; be happy not to be known: hide the little flame of your lamp under the bushel; the least wind would put it out.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Fifth Day, 'The Presentation of Mary in the Temple', meditation III; 7th ed. (1909), p. 33
q.o: Aujourd'hui on ne cherche qu'à paraître ; on veut arriver et jouir tout de suite ; on ne sait pas attendre; on force la plante : elle donne beaucoup tout d'abord ; mais elle s'épuise et meurt au bout de peu de temps. Aimez donc la vie simple et cachée, les emplois modestes de votre position ; soyez heureux de n'être pas connus : cachez sous le boisseau la petite flamme de votre lampe ; le moindre vent l'éteindrait.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: The gratitude of the most holy Virgin breathes forth in acts of love, of praise, of blessing: she exalts the divine goodness. For gratitude is all of that; it is an outpouring into the person of the benefactor; a great, loving outpouring: gratitude is the heart of love!
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Seventh Day, 'The first adorer of the Incarnate Word'; 7th ed. (1909), p. 41
q.o: La reconnaissance de la très sainte Vierge s'exhale en actes d'amour, de louange, de bénédiction : elle exalte la divine bonté. Car la reconnaissance est tout cela; elle est l'expansion en la personne bienfaitrice ; expansion grande, aimante : c'est le cœur de l'amour que la reconnaissance !
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: After all, what does it mean to be interior? It is to love enough to be able to converse and live with Jesus. But Jesus does not make himself heard by the ears, nor seen by the eyes of the body; he speaks only to the recollected soul.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Ninth Day, 'The interior life of Mary', meditation I; 7th ed. (1909), p. 50
q.o: Après tout, qu'est-ce donc qu'être intérieur? C'est aimer assez pour pouvoir causer et vivre avec Jésus. Mais Jésus ne se fait pas entendre aux oreilles, ni voir aux yeux du corps, il parle seulement à l'âme recueillie.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: This is the great secret of perfection: to know how to find it in what is simplest, to know how to nourish it with what is most ordinary, to know how to preserve it in the midst of forgetfulness and indifference.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Tenth Day, 'Modesty, the character of Mary's life'; 7th ed. (1909), p. 55
q.o: Voilà le grand secret de la perfection : savoir la trouver dans ce qui est le plus simple, savoir l'alimenter de ce qui est le plus commun, savoir la conserver au milieu de l'oubli et de l'indifférence.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: Jesus was the centre of love for Mary and Joseph: wheresoever the body shall be, there shall the eagles also be gathered together; where thy treasure is, there is thy heart also. So to have Jesus was the whole centre of these happy parents; they were attached neither to Bethlehem, nor to Nazareth, nor to Egypt: to have Jesus was everything; he was the home of their heart.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Thirteenth Day, 'The life of the Holy Family', meditation I; 7th ed. (1909), p. 67
q.o: Jésus était le centre d'amour de Marie et de Joseph : là où est le corps, les aigles se rassemblent ; là où est le trésor, là est le cœur. De sorte qu'avoir Jésus était tout le centre de ces heureux parents ; on ne tenait ni à Bethléem, ni à Nazareth, ni à l'Egypte : avoir Jésus c'était tout; il était la maison de leur cœur.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: It is because suffering is the law of love: it was Mary's love that made her martyrdom; and because she loved more than any creature, she endured a martyrdom beyond compare. It is also because suffering is the present glorification of Jesus Christ in us: by suffering we continue him, we complete his sacrifice.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Fourteenth Day, 'The compassion of the most holy Virgin', meditation I; 7th ed. (1909), p. 71
q.o: C'est que la souffrance est la loi de l'amour : c'est l'amour de Marie qui a fait son martyre ; et parce qu'elle aimait plus qu'aucune créature, elle a subi un martyre incomparable. — C'est encore que la souffrance est la glorification actuelle de Jésus-Christ en nous : par la souffrance, nous le continuons, nous achevons son sacrifice.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: Love comes from truth known, and a grace of light is worth more than the greatest grace of sweetness and consolation: truth remains, feeling passes.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Twenty-seventh Day, 'The Eucharist, the centre of Mary's life', meditation III; 7th ed. (1909), p. 130
q.o: l'amour vient de la vérité connue, et une grâce de lumière vaut mieux que la plus grande grâce de douceur et de consolation : la vérité demeure, le sentiment passe.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: Jesus has very few adorers who think themselves rewarded enough and happy enough to remain with him, occupied in serving him, like the angels in heaven, like Mary in the Cenacle; he sees at his feet hardly anyone but beggars, or the feverish who ask him for help.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Twenty-eighth Day, 'Mary's life of union with Jesus', meditation III; 7th ed. (1909), p. 134
q.o: Jésus a bien peu d'adorateurs qui s'estiment assez récompensés et assez heureux de demeurer avec lui, occupés à le servir, comme les anges au ciel, comme Marie au Cénacle; il ne voit guère à ses pieds que des mendiants, ou des fiévreux qui lui demandent secours.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: Surely we may rejoice. We do not lose our mother; rather, we send her on ahead of us to prepare our place and to win us claims upon the heart of God.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Thirtieth Day, 'The triumph of Mary' (the Assumption), meditation I; 7th ed. (1909), p. 141
q.o: Certes nous pouvons nous réjouir. Nous ne perdons pas notre mère ; mais nous l'envoyons au-devant de nous pour nous préparer notre place et nous acquérir des droits sur le cœur de Dieu.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: But, O my good Mother, since you deign to become my teacher, you will let me adore Jesus with you, bless him with your praises, pray to him with your prayers, serve him with your hands, love him with your heart, glorify him with your holiness.
q.w: Month of Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament
q.l: Last Day, 'Consecration to Our Lady of the Most Blessed Sacrament', part II; 7th ed. (1909), p. 149
q.o: Mais, ô ma bonne Mère, puisque vous daignez devenir ma maîtresse, vous me laisserez adorer Jésus avec vous, le bénir avec vos louanges, le prier avec vos prières, le servir avec vos mains, l'aimer avec votre cœur, le glorifier avec votre sainteté.
q.oe: Mois de Notre-Dame du T. S. Sacrement, ed. Tesnière (1909)

q.t: All of us are called to set out upon and follow the road to the Jerusalem of glory. God himself has laid it out for us, and that road is none other than love. Like the railways, it has two rails, which are: to love God and to love our neighbour. The locomotive is charity, which runs faster or slower in direct proportion to its degree of heat, that is, of love.
q.w: The Railway, or Means to Attain Happiness (El ferrocarril)
q.l: Colección de opúsculos, vol. III (Barcelona: Librería Religiosa, 1860), 'El ferrocarril', section 'El tren ha…
q.o: Todos los hombres estamos llamados á emprender y seguir el camino de la Jerusalen de la gloria. El mismo Dios nos lo ha trazado, y ese camino no es otro que el amor. Como los caminos de hierro, tiene este dos líneas que son: amar á Dios, y amar al prójimo. La locomotora es la caridad, que anda con celeridad mayor ó menor en razon directa de sus grados de calor, ó sea, de amor.
q.oe: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo (1862) and other works (1858-60)

q.t: Every man must know and continually remember that there is a God infinitely good, wise and almighty; that this God is his Creator, his Preserver, his Redeemer, his Father and his Lord. It is therefore most reasonable that man should love him, serve him and obey him, honouring his holy law, keeping his divine commandments, and directing all his thoughts, words and deeds to his greater honour and glory.
q.w: The Railway Travellers, or A Conversation on the Profanation of Feast Days (Los viajeros del ferrocarril)
q.l: Colección de opúsculos, vol. III (Barcelona: Librería Religiosa, 1860), section 'Deberes del hombre para con Dios', p. 359 (scan PDF p. 362)
q.o: Todo hombre ha de saber y recordar continuamente que hay un Dios infinitamente bueno, sábio y omnipotente; que este Dios es su Criador, su Conservador, su Redentor, su Padre y su Señor. Es, pues, muy racional que el hombre le ame, le sirva y obedezca acatando su santa ley, observando sus divinos preceptos, y dirigiendo todos sus pensamientos, palabras y obras á su mayor honra y gloria.
q.oe: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo (1862) and other works (1858-60)

q.t: We men are all brothers, for we all have one and the same father, who is God; one and the same mother, who is most holy Mary; one and the same redeemer, who is Jesus Christ.
q.w: The Railway Travellers, or A Conversation on the Profanation of Feast Days (Los viajeros del ferrocarril)
q.l: Colección de opúsculos, vol. III (Barcelona: Librería Religiosa, 1860), section 'Deberes del hombre para con sus…
q.o: Todos los hombres somos hermanos, pues todos tenemos un mismo padre, que es Dios; una misma madre, que es María santísima; un mismo redentor, que es Jesucristo.
q.oe: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo (1862) and other works (1858-60)

q.t: We all have to imitate in Saint Joseph the love of work, patience in sickness and persecution, and devotion to most holy Mary; and finally we must all turn to Saint Joseph, that he may protect us in life, and especially at the hour of death.
q.w: The Straight and Sure Road to Heaven (Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo)
q.l: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo, 41st ed. (Barcelona: Librería Religiosa, 1862), 'Devoción á san José', p. 337 (scan PDF p. 342)
q.o: Todos tenemos que imitar de san José el amor al trabajo, la paciencia en las enfermedades y persecuciones, la devocion á María santísima, y finalmente todos hemos de acudir á san José para que nos ampare en vida, y singularmente en la hora de la muerte.
q.oe: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo (1862) and other works (1858-60)

q.t: Rather die than sin. Yes; this is how resolved you must be: to leave everything rather than leave God.
q.w: The Straight and Sure Road to Heaven (Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo)
q.l: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo, 41st ed. (Barcelona: Librería Religiosa, 1862), 'Cinco máximas para…
q.o: Antes morir que pecar. Sí; así debes estar resuelto; dejarlo todo antes que dejar á Dios.
q.oe: Camino recto y seguro para llegar al cielo (1862) and other works (1858-60)

q.t: I want to teach you a way of Christian life that can at the same time make you cheerful and content, and to show you which are the true amusements and the true pleasures, so that you may say with the holy prophet David: Let us serve the Lord in holy joy: Serve ye the Lord with gladness. This is precisely the purpose of this little book: to teach you to serve the Lord and to be cheerful.
q.w: The Companion of Youth (Il giovane provveduto)
q.l: Il giovane provveduto, 101st ed. (Turin, 1885), preface 'Alla gioventù', p. 5 (Opere edite p. [133])
q.o: Io voglio insegnarvi un modo di vita cristiana, che vi possa nel tempo stesso rendere allegri e contenti, e additarvi quali siano i veri divertimenti e i veri piaceri, talchè voi possiate dire col santo profeta Davidde: Serviamo al Signore in santa allegria: Servite Domino in laetitia. Tale appunto è lo scopo di questo libretto: insegnare a servire il Signore e a stare allegri.

q.t: But, some will say, if we start serving the Lord now, we shall become gloomy. Not true: gloomy is he who serves the devil; however hard he tries to look content, he will always have a weeping heart telling him: you are unhappy because you are God's enemy. Who was more affable and jovial than St Aloysius Gonzaga? Who more witty and cheerful than St Philip Neri? Yet their life was a continual practice of every virtue.
q.w: The Companion of Youth (Il giovane provveduto)
q.l: Il giovane provveduto, 1st ed. (Turin: Paravia, 1847), Part I, Article 3 'La salvezza di un figliuolo dipende…
q.o: Ma (taluni diranno) se cominciamo al presente a servire il Signore, diventiamo malinconici. Non è vero, sarà malinconico colui che serve il demonio, il quale comunque si sforzi per mostrarsi contento, tuttavia avrà sempre il cuor che piange, dicendogli: tu sei infelice perchè nemico d'Iddio. Chi più affabile e più gioviale di s. Luigi Gonzaga? Chi più lepido e più allegro di s. Filippo Neri? Nondimeno la loro vita fu una continua pratica di ogni virtù.

q.t: My dear ones, I love you with all my heart, and it is enough that you are young for me to love you very much. In your heart you keep the treasure of virtue: possessing it, you have everything; losing it, you become the unhappiest and most wretched people in the world.
q.w: The Companion of Youth (Il giovane provveduto)
q.l: Il giovane provveduto, 101st ed. (Turin, 1885), preface 'Alla gioventù', p. 7 (Opere edite p. [135])
q.o: Miei cari, io vi amo di tutto cuore, e basta che siate giovani, perchè io vi ami assai. Nel vostro cuore voi conservate il tesoro della virtù, il quale possedendo, avete tutto; perdendolo, voi divenite i più infelici e sventurati del mondo.

q.t: For although He loves all men as the work of His hands, He bears a special affection for the young, so much that He finds His delight in dwelling with them: My delights were to be with the children of men. God loves you because you still have time to do many good works; He loves you because you are at a simple, humble, innocent age, which in general has not yet become the unhappy prey of the infernal enemy.
q.w: The Companion of Youth (Il giovane provveduto)
q.l: Il giovane provveduto, 101st ed. (Turin, 1885), Part I, Article II 'I giovanetti sono grandemente amati da Dio', p. 10 (Opere edite p. [138])
q.o: Imperciocchè quantunque Egli ami tutti gli uomini, come opera delle sue mani, tuttavia porta una particolare affezione ai giovanetti, a segno che Egli trova la sua delizia nel dimorare con essi: Deliciae meae esse cum filiis hominum. Dio vi ama perchè siete ancora in tempo a fare molte opere buone; vi ama perchè siete in una età semplice, umile, innocente, ed in generale non ancora divenuta preda infelice del nemico infernale.

q.t: But remember well that true religion does not consist in words alone; one must come to deeds. So, when you find something worthy of admiration, do not be content to say: this is beautiful, I like this; say rather: I want to strive to do those things which, when I read of them in others, fill me with wonder.
q.w: Life of Dominic Savio (Vita del giovanetto Savio Domenico)
q.l: Vita del giovanetto Savio Domenico (Turin: Paravia, 1859), Bosco's preface 'Giovani carissimi', p. 10 (Opere edite p. [160])
q.o: Ricordatevi però bene che la religione vera non consiste in sole parole; bisogna venir alle opere; quindi, trovando qualche cosa degna di ammirazione, non contentatevi di dire: questo è bello, questo mi piace: dite piuttosto: voglio adoperarmi per fare quelle cose che, lette di altri, mi eccitano alla maraviglia.

q.t: May God give you and all the readers of this little book health and grace to profit from what they will read here; and may the Most Holy Virgin, of whom young Savio was a fervent devotee, obtain for us that we may be of one heart and one soul in loving our Creator, who alone is worthy to be loved above all things and faithfully served all the days of our life.
q.w: Life of Dominic Savio (Vita del giovanetto Savio Domenico)
q.l: Vita del giovanetto Savio Domenico (Turin: Paravia, 1859), Bosco's preface 'Giovani carissimi', closing blessing, p.…
q.o: Dio doni a voi e a tutti i lettori di questo libretto sanità e grazia per trar profitto di quanto ivi andranno leggendo, e la Vergine Santissima, di cui il giovane Savio era fervoroso divoto, ci ottenga di poter fare un cuor solo ed un'anima sola per amare il nostro Creatore, che è il solo degno di essere amato sopra ogni cosa, e fedelmente servito in tutti i giorni di nostra vita.

q.t: The practice of this system rests entirely on the words of St Paul, who says: Charity is kind, is patient; beareth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things. Charity is kind and patient; it suffers all things, but hopes all things and bears any trouble. Therefore only a Christian can successfully apply the Preventive System.
q.w: The Preventive System in the Education of the Young (Il sistema preventivo)
q.l: Il sistema preventivo nella educazione della gioventù, appended to Inaugurazione del Patronato di S.
q.o: La pratica di questo sistema è tutta appoggiata sopra le parole di S. Paolo che dice: Charitas benigna est, patiens est; omnia suffert, omnia sperat, omnia sustinet. La carità è benigna e paziente; soffre tutto, ma spera tutto e sostiene qualunque disturbo. Perciò soltanto il cristiano può con successo applicare il sistema Preventivo.

q.t: Frequent confession, frequent communion and daily Mass are the pillars that must hold up an educational building from which one wishes to keep threats and the rod far away. Never weary the boys nor force them to frequent the holy sacraments, but give them the opportunity to make use of them.
q.w: The Preventive System in the Education of the Young (Il sistema preventivo)
q.l: Il sistema preventivo nella educazione della gioventù, appended to Inaugurazione del Patronato di S.
q.o: La frequente confessione, la frequente comunione, la messa quotidiana sono le colonne che devono reggere un edifizio educativo, da cui si vuole tener lontano la minaccia e la sferza. Non mai annoiare nè obbligare i giovanetti alla frequenza de'santi Sacramenti, ma porgere loro la comodità di approfittarne.

q.t: We are in this world as on a stormy sea, as in an exile, in a valley of tears. Mary is the star of the sea, the comfort in our exile, the light that shows us the way to heaven, drying our tears. And this tender mother does so by obtaining for us continual help, spiritual and temporal.
q.w: The Month of May Consecrated to Mary Most Holy Immaculate (Il mese di maggio)
q.l: Il mese di maggio consacrato a Maria SS. Immacolata (Turin: Paravia, 1858), Day 30 'Maria nostra protettrice nella…
q.o: Noi siamo in questo mondo come in un mar burrascoso, come in un esilio, in una valle di lagrime. Maria è la stella del mare, il conforto nel nostro esilio, la luce che ci addita la via del cielo asciugandoci le lagrime. E ciò fa questa tenera madre coll'ottenerci continui aiuti spirituali e temporali.

q.t: It is in this sacrament that the martyrs found their strength, virgins their fervour, the saints their courage. And we, how often do we approach this heavenly food? If we consider the desires of Jesus Christ and our own need, we must receive Communion very often.
q.w: The Month of May Consecrated to Mary Most Holy Immaculate (Il mese di maggio)
q.l: Il mese di maggio consacrato a Maria SS. Immacolata (Turin: Paravia, 1858), Day 24 'La santa Comunione', no. 2, p. 141 (Opere edite p. [435])
q.o: Egli è in questo sacramento che i martiri trovavano la loro fortezza, le vergini il loro fervore, i santi il loro coraggio. E noi con quale frequenza ci accostiamo a questo cibo celeste? Se esaminiamo i desiderii di Gesù Cristo e il nostro bisogno dobbiamo comunicarci assai sovente.

q.t: Do we like to be learned? Let us go to paradise, and in a moment we shall become more learned than Solomon, more enlightened than all the philosophers; there, in an instant, without tedium and without toil, we shall learn the most sublime sciences. Do we like to gaze on the beauties of creatures? But how much more beautiful must the Creator be?
q.w: The Month of May Consecrated to Mary Most Holy Immaculate (Il mese di maggio)
q.l: Il mese di maggio consacrato a Maria SS. Immacolata (Turin: Paravia, 1858), Day 28 'Del Paradiso', no. 1, p. 160 (Opere edite p. [454])
q.o: Ci piace di essere letterati? Andiamo in paradiso, e in un momento diventeremo più dotti di Salomone, più illuminati di tutti i filosofi; là in un istante senza noia e senza fatica apprenderemo le scienze più sublimi. Ci piace di vagheggiare le bellezze delle creature? ma quanto più bello deve essere il Creatore?

q.t: Let us indeed consider Mary as our mother, and then we shall have some idea of the graces she will obtain for us at the hour of death. Earthly mothers never abandon their children. The more their miseries and ills increase, the more they strive with motherly care to relieve them in the midst of any danger.
q.w: The Month of May Consecrated to Mary Most Holy Immaculate (Il mese di maggio)
q.l: Il mese di maggio consacrato a Maria SS. Immacolata (Turin: Paravia, 1858), Day 31 'Maria nostra protettrice in…
q.o: Di fatti consideriamo Maria come nostra madre, e poi abbiamo una qualche idea delle grazie che ella sarà per ottenerci in punto di morte. Le madri terrene non abbandonano mai i loro figliuoli. Quanto più crescono le loro miserie e i loro mali, tanto più si adoperano con materna sollecitudine per sollevarli in mezzo a qualsiasi pericolo.

q.t: 'Father,' said I, 'do you see, let us say, this vessel lying here to be a little pitcher, or something else?' And he said, 'I see it to be so.' And I replied to him, 'Can it be called by any other name than what it is?' And he said, 'No.' 'Neither can I call myself anything else than what I am, a Christian.'
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 3 (ANF ch. I, §2), her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 19

q.t: Such solicitude I suffered for many days, and I obtained leave for my infant to remain in the dungeon with me; and forthwith I grew strong and was relieved from distress and anxiety about my infant; and the dungeon suddenly became to me as it were a palace, so that I preferred being there to being elsewhere.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 3 (ANF ch. I, §2), her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 23-24

q.t: Then my brother said to me, 'My dear sister, you are already in a position of great dignity, and are such that you may ask for a vision, and that it may be made known to you whether this is to result in a passion or an escape.' And I, who knew that I was privileged to converse with the Lord, whose kindnesses I had found to be so great, boldly promised him, and said, 'To-morrow I will tell you.'
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 4 (ANF ch. I, §3), her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 24-25

q.t: 'Perpetua, I am waiting for you; but be careful that the dragon do not bite you.' And I said, 'In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, he shall not hurt me.' And from under the ladder itself, as if in fear of me, he slowly lifted up his head; and as I trod upon the first step, I trod upon his head.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 4 (ANF ch. I, §3), her first vision (Saturus calls down to her from the top of the ladder), from her own prison diary

q.t: And I went up, and I saw an immense extent of garden, and in the midst of the garden a white-haired man sitting in the dress of a shepherd, of a large stature, milking sheep; and standing around were many thousand white-robed ones. And he raised his head, and looked upon me, and said to me, 'Thou art welcome, daughter.'
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 4 (ANF ch. I, §3), her first vision, from her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 28

q.t: And he called me, and from the cheese as he was milking he gave me as it were a little cake, and I received it with folded hands; and I ate it, and all who stood around said Amen. And at the sound of their voices I was awakened, still tasting a sweetness which I cannot describe.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 4 (ANF ch. I, §3), her first vision (the shepherd in the garden), from her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 28-29

q.t: And I grieved over the grey hairs of my father, that he alone of all my family would not rejoice over my passion. And I comforted him, saying, 'On that scaffold whatever God wills shall happen. For know that we are not placed in our own power, but in that of God.' And he departed from me in sorrow.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 5 (ANF ch. II, §1), her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 31-32

q.t: And my father's misfortune grieved me as if I myself had been beaten, I so grieved for his wretched old age. The procurator then delivers judgment on all of us, and condemns us to the wild beasts, and we went down cheerfully to the dungeon.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 6 (ANF ch. II, §2), her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 33

q.t: After a few days, whilst we were all praying, on a sudden, in the middle of our prayer, there came to me a word, and I named Dinocrates; and I was amazed that that name had never come into my mind until then, and I was grieved as I remembered his misfortune. And I felt myself immediately to be worthy, and to be called on to ask on his behalf.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 7 (ANF ch. II, §3), her own prison diary (Dinocrates was her little brother, who had died aged seven); PL 3, col. 34

q.t: But I trusted that my prayer would bring help to his suffering; and I prayed for him every day until we passed over into the prison of the camp, for we were to fight in the camp-show. Then was the birth-day of Geta Cæsar, and I made my prayer for my brother day and night, groaning and weeping that he might be granted to me.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 7 (ANF ch. II, §3), her own prison diary, praying for her dead brother Dinocrates; PL 3, col. 37-38

q.t: And one drew water from the pool incessantly, and upon its brink was a goblet filled with water; and Dinocrates drew near and began to drink from it, and the goblet did not fail. And when he was satisfied, he went away from the water to play joyously, after the manner of children, and I awoke. Then I understood that he was translated from the place of punishment.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 8 (ANF ch. II, §4), her second vision of Dinocrates, from her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 39

q.t: And he held his hand to me, and we began to go through rough and winding places. Scarcely at length had we arrived breathless at the amphitheatre, when he led me into the middle of the arena, and said to me, 'Do not fear, I am here with you, and I am labouring with you;' and he departed.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 10 (ANF ch. III, §2), her vision on the eve of the games, in which the deacon Pomponius leads her to the arena…

q.t: And I drew near to the trainer and took the branch; and he kissed me, and said to me, 'Daughter, peace be with you:' and I began to go gloriously to the Sanavivarian gate. Then I awoke, and perceived that I was not to fight with beasts, but against the devil. Still I knew that the victory was awaiting me.
q.w: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua's prison diary)
q.l: ch. 10 (ANF ch. III, §2), end of her last vision, from her own prison diary; PL 3, col. 42-43

q.t: Hitherto I have served you as a soldier: allow me now to become a soldier to God: let the man who is to serve thee receive thy donative: I am the soldier of Christ: it is not lawful for me to fight.
q.l: ch. 4 (to Julian Caesar, asking for discharge from the army), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: If this conduct of mine is ascribed to cowardice, and not to faith, I will take my stand unarmed before the line of battle tomorrow, and in the name of the Lord Jesus, protected by the sign of the cross, and not by shield or helmet, I will safely penetrate the ranks of the enemy.
q.l: ch. 4, as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: The Lord Jesus did not predict that he would come clothed in purple, and with a glittering crown upon his head. I will not believe that Christ has come, unless he appears with that appearance and form in which he suffered, and openly displaying the marks of his wounds upon the cross.
q.l: ch. 24 (to the devil, who appeared in royal robes and claimed to be Christ), as recorded by…

q.t: "This," exclaimed he, "is a picture of how the demons act: they lie in wait for the unwary and capture them before they know it: they devour their victims when taken, and they can never be satisfied with what they have devoured."
q.l: Letter III, to Bassula (on seeing water-fowl seizing fish on his last journey), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: O Lord, if I am still necessary to thy people, I do not shrink from toil: thy will be done.
q.l: Letter III, to Bassula (his prayer on his deathbed, when the brethren begged him not to leave them), as recorded by…

q.t: It is not fitting that a Christian should die except among ashes; and I have sinned if I leave you a different example.
q.l: Letter III, to Bassula (refusing straw for his deathbed), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: Allow me, dear brother, to fix my looks rather on heaven than on earth, so that my spirit which is just about to depart on its own journey may be directed towards the Lord.
q.l: Letter III, to Bassula (on his deathbed, asked to turn on his side), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: Why do you stand here, thou bloody monster? Thou shalt find nothing in me, thou deadly one: Abraham's bosom is about to receive me.
q.l: Letter III, to Bassula (his last words, seeing the devil at hand), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: Look at Adam, cast out of Paradise, how he feeds his swine in a garment of skin; but let us, laying aside that old Adam, who still remains in that man, rather put on the new Adam.
q.l: Dialogue II, ch. 10 (on seeing a swineherd clad in skins), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: Let the church both feed and clothe us, as long as we do not appear to have provided, in any way, for our own wants.
q.l: Dialogue III, ch. 14 (after giving a gift of silver to ransom captives), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: If Christ bore with Judas, why should not I bear with Brictio?
q.l: Dialogue III, ch. 15 (his often-repeated saying about the cleric who insulted him), as recorded by Sulpicius Severus

q.t: No; for it was not told me that, 'where he, there thou also'; but 'where thou, there he also'?
q.l: Confessions, Book III, ch. 11 (correcting her son's reading of her dream that he would one day stand where she…)

q.t: Son, for mine own part I have no further delight in any thing in this life. What I do here any longer, and to what I am here, I know not, now that my hopes in this world are accomplished.
q.l: Confessions, Book IX, ch. 10 (at the window in Ostia, after the vision), as recorded by her son St. Augustine

q.t: One thing there was for which I desired to linger for a while in this life, that I might see thee a Catholic Christian before I died. My God hath done this for me more abundantly, that I should now see thee withal, despising earthly happiness, become His servant: what do I here?
q.l: Confessions, Book IX, ch. 10 (at Ostia, a few days before her death), as recorded by her son St. Augustine

q.t: "Lay," she saith, "this body any where; let not the care for that any way disquiet you: this only I request, that you would remember me at the Lord's altar, wherever you be."
q.l: Confessions, Book IX, ch. 11 (her last request to her sons on her deathbed at Ostia), as recorded by her son St.…

q.t: Nothing is far to God; nor was it to be feared lest at the end of the world, He should not recognise whence He were to raise me up.
q.l: Confessions, Book IX, ch. 11 (asked whether she feared to leave her body so far from home), as recorded by her son…

q.t: Whither, father, goest thou without thy son? Whither, holy priest, art thou hastening without thy deacon? Never wast thou wont to offer sacrifice without an attendant.
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §214 (to Pope Sixtus II as he was led to martyrdom; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: Beware lest thy good judgment be endangered, whilst thy fortitude receives its praise. The rejection of a pupil is the loss of the teacher; or how is it that noble and illustrious men gain the victory in the contests of their scholars rather than in their own?
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §214 (to Pope Sixtus II as he was led to martyrdom; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: Abraham offered his son, Peter sent Stephen on before him! Do thou, father, show forth thy courage in thy son. Offer me whom thou hast trained, that thou, confident in thy choice of me, mayest reach the crown in worthy company.
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §214 (to Pope Sixtus II as he was led to martyrdom; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: The flesh is roasted, turn it and eat.
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §216 (on the gridiron; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: I leave thee not nor forsake thee. Greater struggles yet await thee. We as old men have to undergo an easier fight; a more glorious triumph over the tyrant awaits thee, a young man.
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §215 (to his deacon Lawrence on the way to martyrdom; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: Soon shalt thou come. Cease weeping; after three days thou shalt follow me. This interval must come between the priest and his levite. It was not for thee to conquer under the eye of thy master, as though thou neededst a helper.
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §215 (to his deacon Lawrence on the way to martyrdom; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: Why dost thou seek to share in my death? I leave to thee its full inheritance. Why dost thou need my presence? Let the weak disciples go before their master, let the brave follow him, that they may conquer without him. For they no longer need his guidance. So Elijah left Elisha. To thee I entrust the full succession to my own courage.
q.w: On the Duties of the Clergy (his words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 41, §215 (to his deacon Lawrence on the way to martyrdom; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: It would be an injury to my spouse to look on any one as likely to please me. He who chose me first for Himself shall receive me.
q.w: Concerning Virgins (her words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 2, §9 (her answer to the suitors and the executioner; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: Why are you delaying, executioner? Let this body perish which can be loved by eyes which I would not.
q.w: Concerning Virgins (her words as recorded by St. Ambrose)
q.l: Book I, ch. 2, §9 (her answer to the suitors and the executioner; as recorded by St. Ambrose)

q.t: It is the man who, without confession and penance, but carrying with him the defilements of his sins presumes to approach the sacred mysteries, such an one, I say it is, who eats and drinks judgment to himself.
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. II, §19, p. 48: at the council on Easter Communion, as recorded by Turgot

q.t: Whereas we who many days previously have made confession of our sins and have been cleansed from their stains by chastening penance, by trying fasts, by almsgiving and tears—approaching in the Catholic faith to the Lord's Table on the day of His Resurrection, receive the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ, the immaculate Lamb, not to judgment but to the remission of our sins, and as a health-giving preparation for eternal happiness.
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. II, §19, p. 48: at the council on Easter Communion, as recorded by Turgot

q.t: Perhaps on this very day such a heavy calamity may befall the realm of Scotland as has not been for many ages past.
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. IV, §37, p. 73: four days before her death, on the day King Malcolm was killed, as recorded by her chaplain and…

q.t: O unhappy that we are! O guilty that we are! Shall we not be permitted once more to look upon the Holy Cross!
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. IV, §38, p. 76: on her deathbed, while the Black Cross was being brought, as recorded by her chaplain and set…

q.t: I know it, my boy, I know it. By this holy cross, by the bond of our blood, I adjure you to tell me the truth.
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. IV, §40, p. 78: on her deathbed, to her son Edgar, who was hiding the deaths of his father and brother, as…

q.t: I give praise and thanks to Thee, Almighty God, for that Thou hast been pleased that I should endure such deep sorrow at my departing, and I trust that by means of this suffering it is Thy pleasure that I should be cleansed from some of the stains of my sins.
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. IV, §40, p. 79: on hearing that her husband and son had been killed, as recorded by her chaplain and set down by…

q.t: Lord Jesus Christ, who according to the will of the Father, through the co-operation of the Holy Ghost, hast by Thy death given life to the world, deliver me.
q.w: Life of St. Margaret, Queen of Scotland (by Turgot)
q.l: Ch. IV, §41, p. 79: her last words, from the priest's prayer before Communion, as recorded by her chaplain and set…

q.t: Good-by, dear mother. I thank you for all the affection which you have ever shown me, and above all at our last meeting. May God unite us in His Holy Paradise, if we do not see each other again on earth!
q.l: Dieppe, April 6, 1636; Martin, Life of Father Isaac Jogues, tr. Shea (1885), p. 24

q.t: We therefore offered ourselves with our whole heart to the fatherly care of God, as victims immolated to His good pleasure and to His loving displeasure for the salvation of these tribes.
q.l: on being made to run the gauntlet at Ossernenon, August 1642

q.t: I suffered in their sufferings, and the yearnings of my affection were those of a most affectionate father witnessing the sufferings of his own children; for, with the exception of a few old Christians, I had begotten them all to Christ in baptism. However intense my suffering, God granted me strength to console the French and the Hurons who suffered with me.
q.l: on the torture of his Huron and French companions, August 1642

q.t: I wished that wherever I should meet death, which I never lost sight of, it should find me ready, resting on the Holy Scriptures, which had always been my greatest comfort; strengthened with the graces and indulgences of the Most Holy Church, my mother, whom I have always loved, but now more than ever; and lastly, armed with the cross of my Redeemer.
q.l: on the Epistle to the Hebrews and the little wooden cross he kept as a captive among the Mohawks, 1642-43

q.t: I form a resolution, which daily becomes more decided, to remain here as long as it pleases Our Lord, and not to seek to achieve my liberty, even if an opportunity offers. I do not wish to deprive the French, Hurons, and Algonquins of the benefit they receive from my ministry.
q.w: Letter to the Governor of Canada (Montmagny)
q.l: from the Mohawk village, June 30, 1643; Martin, Life of Father Isaac Jogues, tr. Shea (1885), p. 134

q.t: The night I spent in prayer, earnestly imploring our Lord not to let me adopt a conclusion myself, but to give me light to know His most holy will; that in all and through all, even to the stake itself, I would follow it.
q.l: Rensselaerswyck, August 30, 1643, on the Dutch offer to help him escape

q.t: My heart tells me that if I have the happiness of being employed in this mission, Ibo et non redibo; but I shall be happy if our Lord will complete the sacrifice where He has begun it, and make the little blood I have shed in that land the earnest of what I would give from every vein of my body and my heart.
q.w: Letter to a Jesuit Father in France
q.l: 1646, before his last journey to the Mohawks; Martin, Life of Father Isaac Jogues, tr. Shea (1885), p. 198

q.t: In truth, I was sometimes so weary that the body could do no more, but at the same time my soul experienced very deep peace, considering that I was suffering for God; no one knows it if he has not experienced it.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred among the Hurons in the Year 1635
q.l: Ihonatiria, May 27, 1635, on the canoe journey up to the Huron country

q.t: I prostrated myself at once upon my knees to thank God, our Lady, and saint Joseph, for the favors and mercies I had received during the voyage. I saluted the tutelary Angel of the Country, and offered myself to our Lord, with all our little labors, for the salvation of these poor Peoples, taking hope that God would not abandon me there, since he had preserved and led me with so many favors.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred among the Hurons in the Year 1635
q.l: on being left alone on the shore at Toanché, August 5, 1634; Jesuit Relations (Thwaites) 8:91, tr. J. McFie Hunter

q.t: Our hope is in God, and in our Lord Jesus Christ, who shed his blood for the salvation of the Hurons, as well as for the rest of the world.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred among the Hurons in the Year 1635
q.l: Jesuit Relations (Thwaites) 8:151, tr. J. McFie Hunter

q.t: In truth, I feel myself extremely unworthy of this employment; but send holy ones to us, or pray to God our Lord that we may be such as he desires.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred among the Hurons in the Year 1635
q.l: closing of the Relation, Ihonatiria, May 27, 1635; Jesuit Relations (Thwaites) 8:153, tr. J. McFie Hunter

q.t: We had the more need of these exercises, as the high duties we are called upon to perform need more union with God, and because we are compelled to live in a continual bustle. For this reason we often acknowledge that those who come here should bring a good reserve fund of virtue, if they wish here to gather the fruits thereof.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred in the Country of the Hurons in the Year 1636
q.l: ch. II, on the missionaries' annual spiritual exercises

q.t: It is true that fortis ut mors dilectio, the love of God has power to do what death does,—that is to say, to detach us entirely from creatures and from ourselves; nevertheless, these desires that we feel of working for the safety of Infidels are not always sure signs of that pure love.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred in the Country of the Hurons in the Year 1636
q.l: ch. III, 'Important Advice for Those Whom It Shall Please God to Call to New France, and Especially to the Country of the Hurons'

q.t: What a satisfaction to pass these rapids, and to climb these rocks, to him who has before his eyes that loving Savior, harassed by his tormentors and ascending Calvary laden with his Cross
q.w: Relation of What Occurred in the Country of the Hurons in the Year 1636
q.l: ch. III, 'Important Advice for Those Whom It Shall Please God to Call to New France, and Especially to the Country of the Hurons'

q.t: As for the dangers of the soul, to speak frankly, there are none for him who brings to the Country of the Hurons the fear and love of God; on the contrary, I find unparalleled advantages for acquiring perfection. Is it not a great deal to have, in one's food, clothing, and sleep, no other attraction than bare necessity?
q.w: Relation of What Occurred in the Country of the Hurons in the Year 1636
q.l: ch. III, 'Important Advice for Those Whom It Shall Please God to Call to New France, and Especially to the Country of the Hurons'

q.t: God teaches him the beautiful lesson he taught formerly to Saint Catherine of Sienna, to make of his heart a room or temple for him, where he will never fail to find him, as often as he withdraws into it
q.w: Relation of What Occurred in the Country of the Hurons in the Year 1636
q.l: ch. III, 'Important Advice for Those Whom It Shall Please God to Call to New France, and Especially to the Country…

q.t: Certain it is that this Country, or our work here, is much more fitted to feed the soul with the fruits of Heaven than with the fruits of earth. I may be deceiving myself, but I imagine that here is a grand means of increasing the soul in Faith, in Hope, and in Charity.
q.w: Relation of What Occurred in the Country of the Hurons in the Year 1636
q.l: ch. III, 'Important Advice for Those Whom It Shall Please God to Call to New France, and Especially to the Country of the Hurons'

q.t: Jesus, my God and Savior, what can I give Thee in return for all Thou hast given to me? I will take from Thy hand the chalice of suffering, and will invoke Thy name.
q.l: written c. 1640, nine years before his death

q.t: And since Thou hast deigned to die for me, I, therefore, my beloved Jesus, offer Thee from this day forth in the sentiments of joy which I now feel, my body, my blood and my life, in order that I may die for Thee alone, if Thou grantest me that grace. Let me so live that Thou wilt grant me this favor of dying thus happily.
q.l: written c. 1640; as recorded by Paul Ragueneau (Relation of 1649)

q.t: I fear I shall be among the reprobates unless God, who has treated me so gently, will give me an opportunity of suffering.
q.l: found among his writings after his death

q.t: For those who believe falsely, or who do not fill out and adorn their faith with good works (since faith without works dies), neither reign honorably here nor have any share in the eternal kingdom or crown. But if you hold fast the shield of faith, you may have the helmet of salvation as well.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 1, On keeping the Catholic faith; Endlicher 1849, p. 301 (scan rerumhungaricar01endlgoog)
q.o: qui enim falso credunt, uel fidem bonis non implent et ornant operibus, quia fides sine opere moritur, nec hic honeste regnant, nec eterno regno uel corona participant. si uero retinens scutum fidei, habeas eciam galeam salutis.

q.t: For whoever lessens or defiles the dignity of the holy Church is striving to mutilate the body of Christ.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 2, On upholding the state of the Church; Endlicher 1849, p. 302 (scan rerumhungaricar01endlgoog)
q.o: nam qui minuit aut fedat s. ecclesie dignitatem, ille Christi corpus mutilare nititur.

q.t: Indeed, it was above all for this reason that kings were called Augusti: because they augmented the Church. Do the same yourself, so that your crown may be held more praiseworthy, and your life happier and longer.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 2, On upholding the state of the Church; Endlicher 1849, p. 303 (scan rerumhungaricar00hispgoog)
q.o: inde quidem imprimis reges Augusti dicebantur, quia augebant ecclesiam. hec et tu facias , ut et tua corona laudabilior et uita beacior et prolixior habeatur.

q.t: Rule over all of them without anger, pride and envy, peaceably, humbly, gently, always keeping in mind that all men are of one condition, and that nothing exalts but humility, and nothing casts down but pride and envy. If you are peaceable, then you will be called a king and a king's son, and you will be loved by all your knights.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 4, On the honor due to nobles and knights; Migne PL 151, cols. 1239-1240 (scan patrologiaecursu0151mign_i4y5)
q.o: eorum omnibus sine ira et superbia atque invidia pacifice,humiliter,mansuete dominare,memoria retinens semper, quod omnes homines unius sunt conditionis : et quod nil elevat, nisi humilitas : et nihil dejicit, nisi superbia et invidia. Si eris pacificus, tunc diceris rex et regis filius, atque amaberis a cunctis militibus.

q.t: Attend to this, my son: if you wish to have the honor of a kingdom, love justice; if you wish to possess your soul, be patient.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 5, On justice and patience, right after quoting 'In your patience you shall possess your souls'
q.o: Ad hoc tende, fili mi: si vis regni habere honorem, dilige judicium : si animam tuam possidere vis, esto patiens.

q.t: Fear to be a judge; rejoice rather to be a king and to be called one. Patient kings reign; impatient kings play the tyrant.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 5, On justice and patience (advising him to leave capital cases to the judges)
q.o: Time esse judex, gaude vero rex esse et nominari. Reges patientes regnant, impatientes vero tyrannizant.

q.t: For a kingdom of one language and one custom is weak and fragile. Therefore, my son, I bid you to support them with good will and to keep them in honor.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 6, On welcoming and supporting guests (newcomers from other lands)
q.o: nam unius lingue uniusque moris regnum imbecille et fragile est. propterea fili mi iubeo tibi ut bona uoluntate illos nutrias et honeste teneas

q.t: The keeping of prayer is the greatest gain toward a king's salvation; and therefore, in the ninth place, the rule of royal dignity sings: continual prayer is the washing away and remission of sins.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 9, On keeping prayer; Endlicher 1849, p. 307 (scan rerumhungaricar01endlgoog)
q.o: Obseruacio oracionis maxima aquisicio est regalis salutis, et ideo nonum , in nonaria regie dignitatis canit regula : continua oracio est peccatorum ablucio uel remissio.

q.t: Be merciful to all who suffer violence, always keeping in your heart that divine example: I will have mercy and not sacrifice.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 10, On piety, mercy and the other virtues; Endlicher 1849, p. 308 (scan rerumhungaricar00endlgoog)
q.o: sis misericors omnibus uim pacientibus , semper illud diuinum in tuis precordiis habens exemplum : misericordiam uolo et non sacrificium.

q.t: Be patient toward all, not only toward the powerful but also toward those who lack power. Be strong, finally, so that prosperity does not lift you up too much, nor adversity cast you down.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 10, On piety, mercy and the other virtues; Migne PL 151, col. 1242 (scan patrologiaecursu0151mign_i4y5)
q.o: Patiens esto ad omnes, non tantum potentes, sed etiam potestate carentes. Sis denique fortis, ne te prosperitas nimis elevet, aut adversitas dejiciat.

q.t: Be honorable, so that you never willingly bring disgrace upon anyone. Be chaste, so that you shun all the foulness of lust as you would the sting of death.
q.w: Admonitions to his son Emeric (Libellus de institutione morum)
q.l: Chapter 10, On piety, mercy and the other virtues; Endlicher 1849, p. 309 (scan rerumhungaricar00hispgoog)
q.o: sis honestus, ut nunquam alicui spontaneum inferas dedecus. sis pudicus, ut cunctos libidinis fetores sicut stimulum mortis euites.

q.t: Queen of heaven, and my Queen, thus have your soldiers honored the one whom you made king. Had this been done to me by any enemy, I would avenge my wrongs with your help. Knowing, therefore, my Lady, that by this I am sealed with eternal happiness, I rejoice exceedingly.
q.w: Greater Legend of St. Stephen (Legenda maior S. Stephani regis)
q.l: Ch. 13, as recorded by the Legenda maior (c. 1077-83).
q.o: regina celestis et mea, quem tu regem statuisti, milites tui sic honorauerunt. si ab aliquo aduersario mihi hoc illatum fuisset , meas iniurias per tuum ulciscerer adminiculum. sciens ergo domina per hoc eterna me signatum felicitate , nimis exulto

q.t: If it pleases you, Lady of the world, that a part of your inheritance be laid waste by enemies, and that the young planting of Christianity be destroyed, let it not, I pray, be laid to my sloth, but rather to the disposition of your will. If it is the shepherd's fault, let him pay himself what he deserves; but spare, I pray, the innocent sheep.
q.w: Bishop Hartvic, Life of St. Stephen the King (Vita S. Stephani regis)
q.l: Ch. 15, as recorded by Bishop Hartvic (c. 1100), following the Legenda maior, ch. 14.
q.o: si placet tibi domina mundi tue partem hereditatis ab inimicis deuastari, et nouellam plantacionem christianitatis aboleri, non mee precor imputetur desidie, sed pocius disposicioni uoluntatis tue. si pastoris culpa quod meretur ipse luat, insontibus parce precor ouibus.

q.t: He is victor over the world who, while still in the flesh, dies to himself, to his vices, to his passions; no one who spares himself can hate the world, because he must love or hate the world in himself. Only he lives well who either never has to repent or is ever repenting.
q.w: Instructions (Sermons), Instruction III: What is best in the world
q.l: Instruction III (Migne PL 80; Walker's Sermon III), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 102

q.t: O wretched state of man ! We are bound to love that which is far from us and uncomprehended by us and hidden from our eyes while we live in the prison-house of this body. But it will not be always far, and hidden, and unknown; for he would assuredly have been born in vain to whom the eternal were to remain unknown forever.
q.w: Instructions (Sermons), Instruction III: What is best in the world
q.l: Instruction III (Migne PL 80; Walker's Sermon III), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 102

q.t: Let us give back to our God, to our Father, His image undefiled ; let us give it back to Him in holiness, because He is holy; in love, because He is love; in godliness and truth, because He is holiness and truth. Let us not be the painters of an image that is not His! He who is ungovernable, prone to anger, and proud, is painting the image of a tyrant.
q.l: Instruction XI, 'Moyses in lege scripsit' (Migne PL 80; Walker's Sermon XI), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 104

q.t: But what does it profit to know that peace is good, if we do not keep it with all diligence? The best things are commonly also the most fragile, and the more precious a thing is, the greater care must be bestowed upon it. Such a precious and fragile thing is charity.
q.l: Instruction XI (Migne PL 80; Walker's Sermon XI), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 104

q.t: Let each one see to it that for his slandering of others he be not rooted out from the land of the living. No one ever slanders one whom he loves, for slander is the first-born of hate.
