q.l: Instruction XI (Migne PL 80; Walker's Sermon XI), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 105

q.t: What is more emphatically, more repeatedly inculcated by the divine law than love ? And yet, how rarely do we find anyone who fulfills this law? What can we say to excuse ourselves ? Can we say : It is a hard, a toilsome law? But love is not toil; on the contrary, it is sweet; it is a soothing, salutary medicine for the heart.
q.l: Instruction XI (Migne PL 80; Walker's Sermon XI), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 105

q.t: Be gentle in giving, unremitting in charity, just in all things ; forget injuries, but remember benefits. Be obedient to the aged, obliging to the young, not overweening to your equals. Vie with the perfect, never envy those who are better than yourself ; do not be angry with those who have outdistanced you ; do not speak slightingly of those who linger on the way ; give ear to those who urge you on.
q.l: Letter to a young disciple (Migne PL 80, 'Instructio XIV'; Walker's Ep. VI), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 107

q.t: When you are weary and cast down, do not lose heart; weep over your failings, but rejoice in the hope that is in you. Though you see that you are making progress, harbor a wholesome fear of the uncertain issue of life.
q.l: Letter to a young disciple (Migne PL 80, 'Instructio XIV'; Walker's Ep. VI), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 107

q.t: If the shepherd does not hear the voice of the Supreme Shepherd, his own voice will not be heard by his sheep, and what the teacher despises in his own actions, he cannot by his words hold up to others for imitation.
q.w: Letter to the Synod of Gallic Bishops
q.l: Letter to the bishops assembled in synod (c. 603; Walker's Ep. II), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 136

q.t: Let us live with you in this Gaul where we are now, since we are destined to live together in the kingdom of heaven, if we be found worthy to enter therein. For we have one kingdom promised to us and one hope through our calling in Christ Jesus, with whom we shall reign, if we first suffer with Him.
q.w: Letter to the Synod of Gallic Bishops
q.l: Letter to the bishops assembled in synod (c. 603; Walker's Ep. II), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 137

q.t: I have permitted only gentleness to be seen outside, and chained down grief in the depths of my soul. I have tried to keep back my tears rather than to give vent to them ; yet see how they begin to flow in spite of myself. But I must drive them back, for a valiant soldier does not shed tears on the field of battle.
q.w: Letter to the Monks of Luxeuil
q.l: Letter to his monks, written from Nantes on the eve of his expulsion (610; Walker's Ep. IV), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 162

q.t: Our perils are many, the struggle awaiting us is severe, and the enemy terrible; but the recompense is glorious, and the freedom of our will manifest. Without an adversary there is no conflict, and without a conflict there is no crown. Where there is conflict there is courage, vigilance, ardor, endurance, fidelity, wisdom, prudence, firmness. Thus, then, without war no crown, and, I add, without freedom no honor.
q.w: Letter to the Monks of Luxeuil
q.l: Letter to his monks, written from Nantes (610; Walker's Ep. IV), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 163

q.t: Let us, therefore, mount up to the City of God by the royal road of crucifixion of the flesh and contrition of heart; of bodily suffering and humiliation of spirit and conscientious fulfillment of duty; by the grace of Christ, by faith, hope, and charity.
q.w: Letter to the Monks of Luxeuil
q.l: Letter to his monks, written from Nantes (610; Walker's Ep. IV), trans. Metlake 1914, p. 163

q.t: Hence the monk must fast daily, but also daily refresh his body with food; since he must indulge his body, he must do so sparingly and by means of the coarsest food ; for only to this end does he eat daily that he may be able to make daily progress in virtue, pray daily, work daily, and read daily.
q.l: Monastic Rule, ch. 3, Concerning food and drink, trans. Metlake 1914 (his 'free translation'), p. 72

q.t: He who would become a useful guide to souls, and edify them by his speech, must first of all possess in himself the virtues which he is desirous to inspire in them ; without this he will accomplish little. His words will have no effect, unless he appears to practise what he teaches, and to be gifted with even a greater personal sanctity than that which he exacts from others.

He who would qualify himself in study, ought first of all to practise, with a humble heart, the lessons that have been taught him. If contrariwise, he contradicts these by a spirit of pride, he will never acquire the light of intelligence. Jesus Christ, who has taught us humility by His own example, conceals His truth from the proud, and reveals it only to the humble.

But should you meet with opposition in the performance of good works, whether for your own advancement, for God's glory, or the benefit of your neighbour, or even should you be absolutely hindered therefrom, be this on the part of your superiors, your equals, or inferiors, do not dispute with them about it; but hold your peace, and attaching yourself more closely to God, say to Him, " Lord, I suffer violence, answer Thou for me."
q.l: Ch. III, On Purity of Heart (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 152)

q.t: When you are prevented from labouring for God's glory, either by reason of bodily infirmity, or from some other cause which marks His Divine pleasure, be not grieved ; but cast yourself with confidence into the arms of Him who knows what is most to your advantage, and who draws you to Himself in proportion as you abandon yourself without reserve to His direction. Let your chief concern, under these circumstances, be to preserve peace and tranquillity of heart.
q.l: Ch. III, On Purity of Heart (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 152)

q.t: These few reflections with which I have supplied you, will form in you this excellent virtue, which must be regarded as the source, the mother and guardian of all others : I mean humility ; a virtue which, purifying the heart from all vain and useless thoughts, opens the eyes of the soul, and adapts them to the contemplation of the Majesty of God.
q.l: Ch. III, On Purity of Heart (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 156)

q.t: Obedience is the royal road by which man can reach, without obstacle, the summit of that mystical ladder whereon the Lord is seen to rest.
q.l: Ch. IV, Perfection Is More Easily Attained through the Help of a Director (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 159)

q.t: Let it be seen that you speak with the solicitude of a father, so that the penitent may feel in your words the breath of pure charity.

You, then, who desire to benefit others, begin by having recourse to God in the fulness of your heart ; ask Him with simplicity to impart to you this divine charity which embodies in itself the other virtues, and which will enable you to accomplish what you desire.

Hence, the only consolation you should admit into your soul in time of prayer, is that which is produced by the consciousness of your nothingness and misery ; a consciousness which will preserve you in humility, and inspire you with profound reverence for the grandeur and majesty of God, and the desire that he may be honoured and glorified.
q.l: Ch. XII, Remedies against Certain Spiritual Temptations (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 183)

q.t: Two things should follow from what we have said : — the one is to know our own imperfection, our misery, and nothingness ; the other is to renew our endeavours to lead a more perfect life ; so that the desire of perfection may never lose sight of our misery, nor the consciousness of our misery be separated from the desire of perfection.
q.l: Ch. XV, Elucidation and Application of the Motives (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 195)

q.t: Vouchsafe that I may for ever praise and bless Thee with a heart overflowing with joy, and that, obedient to Thee in all things, I may one day taste of the infinite sweetness of Thy eternal banquet, in company with the Angels, the Apostles, and all Thy Saints, however unworthy I am of so great a favour by reason of my ingratitude.
q.l: Ch. XVI, How to Escape the Snares and Temptations of the Devil, from the prayer 'Lord Jesus, grant that by Thy…

q.t: Carry always, then, in the midst of your heart, this God crucified, that He may one day admit you to a participation of His eternal glory. Amen.
q.l: Ch. XIX, Instructions on Various Subjects, closing words (Pradel-Dixon 1875, p. 206)

q.t: Appreciate the honour done you in being employed in education, and look upon the children whom God has confided to you as the children of God Himself. Be much more careful of their education and instruction than you would be, if they were the children of a king.
q.w: Meditations for the Principal Feasts of the Year
q.l: Med. 133, feast of St. Margaret of Scotland (MF 133.2.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'The Christian Teacher', p. 205
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: You are exercising an employment which obliges you to touch hearts ; now, you cannot do it without the Holy Ghost. Ask God to give you the same grace which He bestowed on the Apostles; so that, after having filled you with His Spirit in order to sanctify you, He may also communicate it to you to procure the salvation of others.
q.w: Meditations for All the Sundays of the Year
q.l: Med. 43, Pentecost (MD 43.3.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'The Holy Ghost', p. 354
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: When we have made ourselves voluntarily poor in order to imitate Jesus Christ, we also love, as He did, those whom God has made poor. You have poor children to instruct every day. Love them tenderly, thus imitating the example of Jesus Christ. Prefer them to those who are not poor, because Our Lord does not say that the Gospel is preached to the rich, but to the poor.
q.w: Meditations for the Principal Feasts of the Year
q.l: Med. 166, feast of St. Cyprian (MF 166.2.1-2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'Gratuitousness and Poor Children', p. 169
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: You who have been entrusted with the education of children, should become skilful in the art of speaking to God and speaking of Him ; but rest assured that you will win your pupils over to God but inasmuch as you shall have learned well how to speak to Him and of Him.
q.w: Meditations for All the Sundays of the Year
q.l: Med. 64, 11th Sunday after Pentecost (MD 64.2.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'The Word of God', p. 248
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: You should consider your employment as one of the most considerable and necessary in the Church, where you exercise it in the place of the pastors, fathers and mothers.
q.w: Meditations for the Time of Retreat
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: It is for you who are the masters of those whom you train, to take all possible care to make them really free with the freedom of the children of God, which Jesus Christ merited for us by His death. For this purpose, you have to employ two means with regard to your pupils; the first is meekness and patience ; the second is prudence in reprimands and corrections.
q.w: Meditations for the Time of Retreat
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: In your employment, you should join zeal for the welfare of the Church to that for the good of the state, of which your pupils begin to be members, and should become more perfectly so every day.
q.w: Meditations for the Principal Feasts of the Year
q.l: Med. 160, feast of St. Louis (MF 160.3.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'Employment', p. 138
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: God having given you the grace of living in community, there is nothing that you should more earnestly ask of Him than this union of mind and heart with your Brothers : because it is only by means of this union that you will acquire the peace which should be the happiness of your life. Earnestly beseech the God of hearts that He may make of yours and those of your Brothers but one in that of Jesus.
q.w: Meditations for All the Sundays of the Year
q.l: Med. 39, vigil of the Ascension (MD 39.3.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'Fraternal Charity', p. 41
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: God grants everything to those who pray. He grants nothing to the proud, but He refuses nothing to the humble.
q.w: Meditations for All the Sundays of the Year
q.l: Med. 38, Rogation Tuesday (MD 38.3.1); Extracts 1910, ch. 'God', p. 107
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: The more humble we are, the greater things will God do in us.
q.w: Meditations for the Principal Feasts of the Year
q.l: Med. 79, feast of St. Francis Xavier (MF 79.2.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'Humility', p. 173
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: We are happy in this world only inasmuch as we think of God and love Him. It appears that your love for God is very feeble ; I am not surprised, when you tell me that you rarely think of God. How can you expect it to be otherwise ?
q.l: Letter to a Brother, as given in Extracts 1910, ch. 'The Presence of God', p. 310
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: It is inconceivable how much Our Lord loves those who leave everything for love of Him, and how many graces He grants them both for themselves and others. As their hearts are void of the things of this world, He fills them with His Holy Spirit, because the more we leave for Him exteriorly the more He gives interiorly.
q.w: Meditations for the Principal Feasts of the Year
q.l: Med. 167, feast of St. Matthew (MF 167.2.1); Extracts 1910, ch. 'Our Lord Jesus Christ', p. 178
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: If Mary received a great abundance of grace, it is for the purpose of sharing it with those who have recourse to her. Avail yourself, therefore, by your zeal for her honour and by your recourse to her protection, of the advantages offered you.
q.w: Meditations for the Principal Feasts of the Year
q.l: Med. 163, Nativity of the Blessed Virgin (MF 163.3.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'The Most Blessed Virgin', p. 383
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: Abandon yourself entirely to the guidance of Our Lord, allowing Him to reign over all your interior movements in a manner so absolute on His part and so dependent on yours, that you may really be able to say, that it is no longer you who live but that it is Jesus Christ who liveth in you.
q.w: Meditations for All the Sundays of the Year
q.l: Printed as 'Med. 29' in Extracts 1910 (ch. 'Our Lord Jesus Christ', p. 180)
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: Never complain when you are in pain, either interior or exterior; and rest assured that the more you suffer, the more means you will have of belonging to God.
q.w: Meditations for All the Sundays of the Year
q.l: Med. 35, 4th Sunday after Easter (MD 35.3.2); Extracts 1910, ch. 'Spiritual Consolation', p. 85
q.tr: the Brothers of the Christian Schools

q.t: Christians, remember, when you go to the confessional, that you go but to wash yourselves, and to wash in the Wounds and the Blood of Jesus Christ.
The durability of a building depends upon the solidity of the foundation. Likewise a Christian soul cannot persevere, except by founding all her actions in the simplicity and truth of God.
Compassion is the daughter of Charity. All things must be done in charity and for charity, serving our neighbor as we do God Himself, Who regards as done to Himself whatever is done to His members.
q.l: Part II, Third Section, Sayings Concerning Various Virtues, no. 26 (p. 424)

q.t: The silence of the lips suffices not, if the silence of the heart is not kept.
q.l: Part II, Third Section, Sayings Concerning Various Virtues, no. 29 (p. 424)

q.t: When it seems to you, dearest sister, that the little boat of your soul is about to sink, throw into the sea the anchor of hope, placing all your confidence in the Divine help, and have no fear lest God will fail to meet your confidence. He so loves our souls that He grants more than we ask.
q.l: Letter 3, to Sr. Maria Fedele Soldani and Sr. Diamante Mazzinghi of San Giovannino, Florence, 12 August 1592 (p. 428)

q.t: Sit in your cell as in paradise. Cast the whole world behind you and out of your memory, keeping watch over your thoughts as a good fisherman watches over the fish. The one way is in the psalms; do not leave it.
q.w: The Brief Rule (in Bruno of Querfurt, Life of the Five Brothers)
q.l: Vita quinque fratrum, final chapter, MGH SS 15.2 p. 738, lines 23-25: the brief rule John received from his master…
q.o: Sede in cella quasi in paradiso; proice post tergum de memoria totum mundum, cautus ad cogitationes, quasi bonus piscator ad pisces. Una via est in psalmis; hanc ne dimittas.

q.t: Oh, how well hermits could dwell in these secluded recesses of the woods! How fittingly they could rest here, free from all the disturbance of worldly noise!
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 1, PL 144:955B: what he said to himself as a young man hunting in the woods, as recorded by…
q.o: O quam bene poterant eremitae in his nemorum recessibus habitare! quam congrue possent hic ab omni saecularis strepitus perturbatione quiescere!

q.t: It is better, if possible, to sing one psalm from the heart and with compunction than to run through a hundred while the mind chatters idly.
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 9, PL 144:964C: his habitual teaching ('Dicebat etiam...'), reported speech as recorded by St.…
q.o: melius esse, si possibile sit, unum psalmum ex corde et cum compunctione cantare quam centum cum mentis fabulatione percurrere.

q.t: Dear Jesus, beloved Jesus, why hast thou forsaken me? Hast thou wholly delivered me into the hands of my enemies?
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 16, PL 144:969B: his cry when beaten by demons in his cell at Classe, as recorded by St. Peter…
q.o: Chare Jesu, dilecte Jesu, quare me dereliquisti? Nunquid omnino me inimicorum manibus tradidisti?

q.t: Behold, I am ready; come! If there is any strength in you, show it. Are you already utterly spent? Are you already beaten, and have you no more engines of war to use against this little servant of God?
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 17, PL 144:970A: his challenge to the evil spirits that appeared around his cell, as recorded…
q.o: Ecce paratus sum, venite; et si quae in vobis est virtus, ostendite. Nunquid jam omnino deficitis? nunquid jam victi estis, et aliquas contra Dei servulum certandi machinas non habetis?

q.t: If you carry the cross of Christ, it remains for you not to abandon the obedience of Christ. Go, therefore: obtain the consent of your own abbot, return, and live humbly under his authority, so that the building of holy work, which good will builds and humility raises up, the virtue of obedience may lift on high.
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 24, PL 144:974C: his counsel to the hermit Venerius, who lived under no superior, as recorded…
q.o: Si crucem Christi portas, superest ut Christi obedientiam non relinquas. Vade igitur, et consensu a proprio abbate suscepto, revertere, et sub ejus dominio humiliter vive; quatenus sacri operis aedificium, quod bona voluntas aedificat, humilitas erigit, obedientiae virtus extollat.

q.t: Dear Jesus, dear one, my sweet honey, ineffable desire, sweetness of the saints, delight of the angels!
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 31, PL 144:983A: what he cried out when rapt in contemplation, as recorded by St. Peter Damian
q.o: Chare Jesu, chare, mel meum dulce, desiderium ineffabile, dulcedo sanctorum, suavitas angelorum

q.t: I too, brothers, do not know what to do with so wicked a man. Shall we put out his eyes? But then he will not see. Shall we cut off his hand? But then he can no longer work, and so perhaps he will starve. Shall we cut off his foot? He will not be able to walk. Rather, bring him in and first set food before him, so that meanwhile we may decide what to do with him.
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 36, PL 144:987C: spoken 'cheerfully' to the brothers who had caught a thief breaking into a cell
q.o: Et ego, fratres, ignoro quid de tam malo homine possimus facere. Eruimus sibi oculos? sed postea non videbit. Incidimus ei manum? sed amplius non laborabit, ac per hoc forsitan fame peribit. Si pedem truncamus? ambulare non poterit. Sed intro eum minate, et cibum illi prius apponite, ut quid de eo faciendum sit, interim pertractemus.

q.t: I perceive that it is by no means the judgment of God's will that I should go any further. Yet, since I know the desire of your intention, I compel none of you to turn back. For many before us, too, have striven with vows and efforts to reach the summit of martyrdom; but because divine providence judged otherwise, they were obliged to remain in their own station.
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 39, PL 144:989C: to his disciples when illness stopped his missionary journey to Hungary, as…
q.o: Perpendo, inquit, nequaquam divinae voluntatis esse judicium ut ultra progrediar. Verumtamen, quia intentionis vestrae desiderium non ignoro, neminem vestrum redire compello. Multi nempe etiam ante nos votis et nisibus studuerunt ad martyrii culmen pertingere, sed quia divina providentia aliter sensit, in suo gradu coacti sunt remanere.

q.t: I know a man in Christ whose soul was carried before God shining like snow, in human form, and of the stature of full maturity.
q.w: Life of St. Romuald (St. Peter Damian)
q.l: Vita S. Romualdi, ch. 51, PL 144:996B: his answer to disciples who asked in what form the soul appears at judgment…
q.o: Scio hominem in Christo, cujus anima delata est ante Deum splendida velut nix, humana quidem effigie, statura vero perfectae aetatis.

q.t: How shall this be done, because I know not man?
Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name.

And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away.
He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever.
Son, why hast thou done so to us? behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.
They have no wine.
Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.
Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God.
Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we have believed and have known, that thou art the Christ, the Son of God.
Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
Lord, save me.
Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.
Lord, thou knowest all things: thou knowest that I love thee.
Do penance, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of your sins: and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
Silver and gold I have none; but what I have, I give thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise, and walk.
Neither is there salvation in any other. For there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved.
We ought to obey God, rather than men.
In very deed I perceive, that God is not a respecter of persons. But in every nation, he that feareth him, and worketh justice, is acceptable to him.
But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people: that you may declare his virtues, who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light
But sanctify the Lord Christ in your hearts, being ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you.
But before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves: for charity covereth a multitude of sins.

Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you. Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour. Whom resist ye, strong in faith
Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?
That they should seek God, if happily they may feel after him or find him, although he be not far from every one of us: For in him we live, and move, and are

But I fear none of these things, neither do I count my life more precious than myself, so that I may consummate my course and the ministry of the word which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
remember the word of the Lord Jesus, how he said: It is a more blessed thing to give, rather than to receive.

Charity is patient, is kind: charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely; is not puffed up; Is not ambitious, seeketh not her own, is not provoked to anger, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth with the truth; Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.
And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me. And that I live now in the flesh: I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and delivered himself for me.
For to me, to live is Christ; and to die is gain.
I can do all these things in him who strengtheneth me.
And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good

For I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor might, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me. For which cause I please myself in my infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ. For when I am weak, then am I powerful.
But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ; by whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.

Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil. For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and power, against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness in the high places.
Be not overcome by evil, but overcome evil by good.

I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. As to the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord the just judge will render to me in that day: and not only to me, but to them also that love his coming.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
It is the Lord.
But these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God: and that believing, you may have life in his name.
That God is light, and in him there is no darkness.
Behold what manner of charity the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called, and should be the sons of God.
My little children, let us not love in word, nor in tongue, but in deed, and in truth.
God is charity: and he that abideth in charity, abideth in God, and God in him.
Fear is not in charity: but perfect charity casteth out fear

Let us therefore love God, because God first hath loved us. If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar. For he that loveth not his brother, whom he seeth, how can he love God, whom he seeth not?
this is the victory which overcometh the world, our faith.
to beseech you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.

But you, my beloved, building yourselves upon your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, Keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, unto life everlasting.

Now to him who is able to preserve you without sin, and to present you spotless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, in the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, To the only God our Saviour through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory and magnificence, empire and power, before all ages, and now, and for all ages of ages. Amen.
Let us also go, that we may die with him.
Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?
Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.
My Lord, and my God.
We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.
There is a boy here that hath five barley loaves, and two fishes; but what are these among so many?
We have found him of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets did write, Jesus the son of Joseph of Nazareth.
Come and see.
Lord, shew us the Father, and it is enough for us.
Rabbi, thou art the Son of God, thou art the King of Israel.

It seemed good to me also, having diligently attained to all things from the beginning, to write to thee in order, most excellent Theophilus, That thou mayest know the verity of those words in which thou hast been instructed.
The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.
Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
Lord, hast thou no care that my sister hath left me alone to serve? speak to her therefore, that she help me.
Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. But now also I know that whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee.
I know that he shall rise again, in the resurrection at the last day.
Yea, Lord, I have believed that thou art Christ the Son of the living God, who art come into this world.
Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
Because they have taken away my Lord; and I know not where they have laid him.
Sir, if thou hast taken him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
Rabboni (which is to say, Master).
I have seen the Lord
I am Gabriel, who stand before God: and am sent to speak to thee, and to bring thee these good tidings.
Fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John
Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.

Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God. Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son; and thou shalt call his name Jesus. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the most High; and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father; and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever. And of his kingdom there shall be no end.
The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee. And therefore also the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
Because no word shall be impossible with God.
Bless ye the God of heaven, give glory to him in the sight of all that live, because he hath shewn his mercy to you.
For it is good to hide the secret of a king: but honourable to reveal and confess the works of God.

Prayer is good with fasting and alms more than to lay up treasures of gold: For alms delivereth from death, and the same is that which purgeth away sins, and maketh to find mercy and life everlasting.
When thou didst pray with tears, and didst bury the dead, and didst leave thy dinner, and hide the dead by day in thy house, and bury them by night, I offered thy prayer to the Lord.
For I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven, who stand before the Lord.
Peace be to you, fear not. For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God: bless ye him, and sing praises to him.
It is time therefore that I return to him that sent me: but bless ye God, and publish all his wonderful works.
Be of good courage, thy cure from God is at hand.
The Lord command thee.
How long do you halt between two sides? if the Lord be God, follow him

O Lord God of Abraham, and Isaac, and Israel, shew this day that thou art the God of Israel, and I thy servant, and that according to thy commandment I have done all these things. Hear me, O Lord, hear me: that this people may learn, that thou art the Lord God, and that thou hast turned their heart again.
It is enough for me, Lord, take away my soul: for I am no better than my fathers.
With zeal have I been zealous for the Lord God of hosts

Neither dost thou fear God, seeing thou art condemned under the same condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward of our deeds; but this man hath done no evil. And he said to Jesus: Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom.
If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there.
Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
I indeed baptize you in the water unto penance, but he that shall come after me, is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear; he shall baptize you in the Holy Ghost and fire.
I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?
I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias.
Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world.
And I saw, and I gave testimony, that this is the Son of God.
A man cannot receive any thing, unless it be given him from heaven.
the friend of the bridegroom, who standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth with joy because of the bridegroom's voice. This my joy therefore is fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.
He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do in like manner.

Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed art thou that hast believed, because those things shall be accomplished that were spoken to thee by the Lord.
Not so; but he shall be called John.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people: And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant: As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning: Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us:

To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament, The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us, That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days.

And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways: To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins: Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us: To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: to direct our feet into the way of peace.

Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace; Because my eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples: A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.

Behold this child is set for the fall, and for the resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign which shall be contradicted; And thy own soul a sword shall pierce, that, out of many hearts, thoughts may be revealed.
For so the Lord hath commanded us: I have set thee to be the light of the Gentiles; that thou mayest be for salvation unto the utmost part of the earth.

Ye men, why do ye these things? We also are mortals, men like unto you, preaching to you to be converted from these vain things, to the living God, who made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all things that are in them
through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
Our lord Pope Alexander is dead, and his death has fallen upon me, shaking my whole inmost being and throwing it into utter turmoil.
q.w: Letter to Abbot Desiderius of Monte Cassino on his election
q.o: Dominus noster papa Alexander mortuus est, cujus mors super me cecidit, et omnia viscera mea concutiens, penitus conturbavit.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: We ought, my daughter, to take refuge in this singular sacrament, to seek this singular remedy.
q.w: Letter to Countess Matilda of Tuscany
q.l: Register 1.47 (1074), on frequent Communion; Migne PL 148, col. 328A
q.o: Debemus, o filia, ad hoc singulare confugere sacramentum, singulare appetere medicamentum.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: And of the Mother of the Lord, to whom above all I have entrusted you, and do entrust you, and shall never cease to entrust you until we see her as we long to, what shall I tell you, she whom heaven and earth never cease to praise, though they cannot praise her as she deserves?
q.w: Letter to Countess Matilda of Tuscany
q.o: De Matre vero Domini, cui te principaliter commisi et committo, et nunquam committere, quousque illam videamus, ut cupimus, omittam, quid tibi dicam, quam coelum et terra laudare, licet ut meretur nequeant, non cessant?
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: But hold this beyond all doubt: that as she is higher and better and holier than every mother, so much the more merciful and tender is she toward sinners, men and women, who turn back to God.
q.w: Letter to Countess Matilda of Tuscany
q.o: Hoc tamen procul dubio teneas, quia, quanto altior et melior ac sanctior est omni matre, tanto clementior et dulcior circa conversos peccatores et peccatrices.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: For we believe there can be no doubt of the salvation of a woman who is known to serve, from the heart, humility and love, in which the whole law is contained.
q.w: Letter to Queen Matilda of England
q.o: Non quippe dubitandum de ejus salute fore credimus, quae humilitati et dilectioni, in qua lex ex toto continetur, ex corde inservire dignoscitur.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: For I have often asked him, as far as he granted me, either to take me from this present life or to make me of use to our common mother; and yet he has not yet delivered me from great tribulation, nor has my life been of use, as I hoped, to that mother to whom he has bound me with his chains.
q.w: Letter to Abbot Hugh of Cluny
q.o: Ego enim saepe illum rogavi, prout ipse dedit, ut aut me de praesenti vita tolleret, aut matri communi per me prodesset, et tamen de magna tribulatione adhuc non eripuit, neque vita mea praedictae matri, cujus me catenis alligavit, ut sperabam, profuit.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: When I come back to myself, I find myself so weighed down by the burden of my own deeds that no hope of salvation remains, save in the mercy of Christ alone.
q.w: Letter to Abbot Hugh of Cluny
q.o: Ad meipsum cum redeo, ita me gravatum propriae actionis pondere invenio ut nulla remaneat spes salutis, nisi de sola misericordia Christi.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: For if I did not hope to come to a better life and to be of use to holy Church, I would by no means remain in Rome, where, God is my witness, I have lived under constraint these twenty years. So it is that, between the sorrow renewed in me every day and the hope that, alas, is drawn out too long, shaken by a thousand storms, I live on somehow, as one who is dying.
q.w: Letter to Abbot Hugh of Cluny
q.o: Nam si non sperarem ad meliorem vitam, et utilitatem sanctae Ecclesiae venire, nullo modo Romae, in qua coactus, Deo teste, jam a viginti annis inhabitavi, remanerem. Unde fit ut inter dolorem qui quotidie in me renovatur, et spem quae nimis, heu, protenditur, mille quassatus tempestatibus quoquomodo moriens vivo.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: This charity, then, we and you owe to one another more especially than to other peoples, since we believe in and confess one God, albeit in different ways, and every day praise and worship him as the Creator of the ages and the Ruler of this world.
q.w: Letter to al-Nasir (Anzir), ruler of Mauretania
q.l: Register 3.21 (1076); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865), p. 237 (= Migne PL 148, col. 451A)
q.o: Hanc itaque caritatem nos et vos specialius nobis quam caeteris gentibus debemus, qui unum Deum, licet diverso modo, credimus et confitemur, qui eum creatorem saeculorum et gubernatorem huius mundi cotidie laudamus et veneramur.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: For God knows that we love you purely for the honor of God, and that we desire your salvation and honor in the present life and in the life to come. And with heart and lips we pray that God himself, after the long span of this life, may lead you into the bosom of blessedness of the most holy patriarch Abraham.
q.w: Letter to al-Nasir (Anzir), ruler of Mauretania
q.o: Scit enim Deus quia pure ad honorem Dei te diligimus, et salutem et honorem tuum in praesenti et in futura vita desideramus. Atque ut ipse Deus in sinum beatitudinis sanctissimi patriarchae Abrahae post longa hujus vitae spatia te perducat corde et ore rogamus.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: For the more the glory of this life is sought, the less the glory of the life to come is desired. That woman is truly called a queen before God who rules her conduct in the fear and love of Christ.
q.w: Letter to a queen, his daughter in Christ (A.)
q.o: Quanto enim hujus vitae gloria quaeritur, tanto minus futurae desideratur. Illa enim mulier vere apud Deum regina dicitur, quae mores suos in timore et amore Christi moderatur.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: For ever since, by divine disposition, Mother Church set me upon the apostolic throne, though I was most unworthy and, as God is my witness, unwilling, my chief care has been that holy Church, the bride of God, our lady and mother, should return to her own true beauty and remain free, chaste, and catholic.
q.l: Epistolae extra Registrum 64 (Salerno, 1084); Migne PL 148, col. 709D
q.o: Ex quo enim dispositione divina mater Ecclesia in throno apostolico me valde indignum, et Deo teste invitum collocavit, summopere procuravi, ut sancta Ecclesia sponsa Dei Domina, et mater nostra, ad proprium rediens decus, libera, et casta, et catholica permaneret.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: Who are they, or how many, who for the fear or the love of almighty God, in whom we live, and move, and are, toil as hard, or labor even unto death, as worldly soldiers do for their lords, or even for their friends and dependents?
q.l: Epistolae extra Registrum 64 (Salerno, 1084); Migne PL 148, col. 709C
q.o: Qui, vel quoti sunt, qui pro timore, vel amore omnipotentis Dei, in quo vivimus, movemur et sumus, tantum desudent, vel usque ad mortem laborent, quantum saeculares milites pro dominis suis, vel etiam pro amicis et subditis?
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: I have loved justice and hated iniquity: therefore I die in exile.
q.l: As recorded by Paul of Bernried, Life of Gregory VII, ch. 12, §102 (Salerno, 25 May 1085); Migne PL 148, col. 95A
q.o: Dilexi justitiam, et odivi iniquitatem, propterea morior in exsilio.
q.oe: Migne, Patrologia Latina 148 (1853); Jaffé, Monumenta Gregoriana (1865)

q.t: This yoke no malicious tale has unloosed from my neck, no long absence from my land has broken it nor ever shall destroy it, though I should be removed from thee by the whole span of space and time. Never shall I live separate from thee in soul: sooner shall life itself depart from my frame than thy face from my heart.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXX, lines 44-48 (= Paulinus, Carmen 11); the yoke is their friendship

q.t: Through all the length of time given to mortals and ordained, so long as I shall be confined in this halting frame, though I be held a world apart, thee neither parted by a world nor severed from my sight I will keep implanted in my inmost being: in heart I shall see thee, in loving thought embrace thee, having thee with me everywhere.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXX, lines 49-56 (= Paulinus, Carmen 11)

q.t: And when, released from the prison of the body, I shall have flown forth from the earth, in whatever clime our general Father shall place me, there also will I bear thee in my heart; nor shall the selfsame end which severs me from my body, unloose me from love of thee.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXX, lines 57-62 (= Paulinus, Carmen 11)

q.t: Why dost thou bid the deposed Muses return to my affection, my father? Hearts consecrate to Christ give refusal to the Camenae, are closed to Apollo.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 19-22 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: Now 'tis another force governs my heart, a greater God, who demands another mode of life, claiming for himself from man the gift he gave, that we may live for the Father of life.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 29-32 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: For what good thing or true can they hold who hold not the head of all, God, the enkindler and source of the good and true, whom no man seeth save in Christ.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 43-46 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: He is the light of truth, the path of life, the strength, mind, hand, and power of the Father, the sun of righteousness, the fount of blessings, the flower of God, born of God, creator of the world, life of our mortality and death of Death. He, the Lord of Virtues, to us God and for us Man, puts on our nature as we must put on his, linking God with man in perpetual intercourse, himself of each partaking.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 47-56 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: Those aimless surges, which the toils of life stir up in the course of this present span of time, are brought to naught by faith in a life to come with God.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 67-69 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: Wherefore thou shouldst give thanks rather than complain because I—that son of thine, offspring of thy learning and thy character, Paulinus, whose parentage thou dost not deny, even now when thou believest me wayward—have so changed my principles that I have gained grace to become the child of Christ while I am the child of Ausonius. He will confer his rewards upon thy merit and from this tree of thine proffer the first fruit to thee.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 147-153 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: I would that jealousy with good grounds may begin to pluck at me: bearing the name of Christ I shall welcome taunts. A mind strengthened by power divine feels no weak shame, and the praise I here despise is restored to me when Christ is judge.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 185-188 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: That I am foolish in the eyes of those who follow other aims gives me no pause, if only in sight of the eternal King my opinion be wise. A short-lived thing is man at best, man with his frail body and passing season, dust and a shadow without Christ: his praise and blame are so much worth as the arbiter himself.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 286-290 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: And unless, while this present time is granted, we take careful heed to live according to the command of Christ our Lord, too late, when man has put off his mortal frame, will be his complaint that while he feared the light rebuke of human tongues, he feared not the severe wrath of the Heavenly Judge.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 293-297 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: And that He sitteth on the throne at the right hand of the eternal Father, that He is set over all as king, and that as years roll away He will come to try all races with even-balanced judgment, and bestow due rewards upon their several deeds, I for my part believe, and, fearing, toil with restless zeal that, if so it may be, I be not cut off by death ere I am cut off from sin.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 298-303 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: This is my fear, this my task, that the Last Day overtake me not asleep in the black darkness of profitless pursuits, spending wasted time amid empty cares.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 316-318 (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: If this thou dost approve, rejoice in thy friend's rich hope: if otherwise, leave me to be approved by Christ alone.
q.l: Loeb Ausonius II, Epistle XXXI, lines 330-331, closing lines (= Paulinus, Carmen 10)

q.t: And I want you to know, dearest brother, concerning the faith of which you wrote, and the false slanders they put forward against the truth, that, helped by your prayers and those of all the faithful Christians who are with you, living and dying I will defend the faith of our salvation.
q.l: Epistle 14, to Theodore, written as a prisoner (653-654); Migne PL 87, col. 198D
q.o: Et scire te volo, dilectissime frater, de fide quam significasti, nec non et falsis calumniis, quas adversum veritatem proponunt, quia opitulantibus nobis orationibus vestris, ac omnium fidelium Christianorum, qui vobiscum sunt, et vivens et moriens salutis nostrae fidem defendam

q.t: As for our Lady, the glorious ever-virgin Mary, who gave birth to our God and Lord Jesus Christ, and whom all the holy and catholic Fathers call the Mother of God, since she bore God made man: wicked men have borne false witness against me, or rather against their own souls.
q.l: Epistle 14, to Theodore, written as a prisoner (653-654); Migne PL 87, col. 199A-200A
q.o: Porro de domina nostra gloriosa semper virgine Maria, quae Deum et Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum peperit, quam omnes sancti et catholici Patres Dei genitricem appellant, ut pote quae Deum hominem genuit, falsum contra me, imo contra suas ipsorum animas iniqui viri testificati sunt.

q.t: Your dear charity has wished to know how I was carried off from the see of the holy apostle Peter, like a lonely sparrow from the house.
q.w: Letter to Theodore on his seizure in Rome
q.l: Epistle 15, to Theodore, written as a prisoner (653-654); Migne PL 87, col. 199B
q.o: Noscere voluit cara vestra dilectio qualiter de sede sancti Petri apostoli, sicut unus passer solitarius ab aedificio, raptus fuerim.

q.t: As for our not having been prepared to resist: I judged it better to die ten times over than that the blood of any single person should be shed upon the ground.
q.w: Letter to Theodore on his seizure in Rome
q.l: Epistle 15, to Theodore; Migne PL 87, col. 201A
q.o: Quod autem praeparati non fuerimus ad repugnandum, melius judicavi decies mori, quam unius cujuscusque sanguinem in terram fundi.

q.t: In that same hour, therefore, I gave myself up to be brought before the emperor, and not to resist. And when, to tell the truth, some of the clergy cried out to me not to do this, I lent my ear to none of them, lest killings should suddenly break out.
q.w: Letter to Theodore on his seizure in Rome
q.l: Epistle 15, to Theodore; Migne PL 87, col. 201B
q.o: Eadem itaque hora dedi meipsum ad exhibendum imperatori, et non resistendum. Porro acclamantibus mihi, ut veritatem dicam, quibusdam ex clero ne facerem hoc, nulli eorum accommodavi aurem, ne subito fierent homicidia.

q.t: For as in wintertime, when the wind blows hard, the leaves are shaken from the trees and fall, so the candles of the holy church were struck by their weapons and, beaten down, were dashed to the pavement; and a sound was heard in that church like some terrible thunder, both from the clash of arms and from the multitude of candles they had broken.
q.w: Letter to Theodore on his seizure in Rome
q.l: Epistle 15, to Theodore, on the soldiers entering the Lateran basilica; Migne PL 87, col. 200D-201A
q.o: Quemadmodum namque in hiemali tempore vento valide flante folia ex arboribus concussa cadunt, ita percutiebantur armis candelae sanctae ecclesiae, et retunsae excutiebantur in pavimentum; et audiebatur sonitus qui in eadem fiebat ecclesia, veluti tonitrus quidam horribilis tam ex pressura armorum, quam ex multitudine candelarum ab eis fractarum.

q.t: But I believe in the power of God, who beholds all things, that when I have been taken from this present life, account will be asked of all who persecute me, so that, led at least in this way to repentance, they may be converted from their iniquity.
q.w: Letter to Theodore on his seizure in Rome
q.l: Epistle 15, to Theodore; Migne PL 87, col. 202C
q.o: Sed credo in virtutem Dei qui omnia conspicit, quia cum de praesenti vita subductus fuero, exquirentur de his omnibus qui me persequuntur, ut saltem sic ad poenitentiam ducti, ab iniquitate sua convertantur.

q.t: And when we asked, we learned from the bearer of this letter that he had brought nothing here from Italy; and I marveled, and glorified my God even in this, for he apportions our tribulations as he knows best, above all since the famine and want in this land are such that bread is only spoken of here, but never seen at all.
q.w: Letter from exile in the Crimea to a beloved friend
q.o: Et cum interrogassemus, cognovimus ab eo, quod nihil huc detulerit ab Italia; et miratus sum, et glorificavi Deum meum etiam in hoc, quoniam, sicut scit, tribulationes nostras dispensat maxime cum fames in hac terra et necessitas talis esset, ut panis in ea tantum nominetur, non tamen penitus videatur.

q.t: For unless provisions are sent to us from those parts, or from the region of Pontus, we cannot live here at all. For the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh weak, as you yourself also know.
q.w: Letter from exile in the Crimea to a beloved friend
q.o: Quoniam nisi mittantur nobis ex partibus illis sumptus, vel a partibus Ponti, hic vivere omnino nequimus. Spiritus enim promptus est, caro vero infirma, ut etiam ipse nosti.

q.t: For if Saint Peter so refreshes strangers there, that is, at Rome, what shall we say of ourselves, who are his own servants, who have served him if only for a moment, and who now stand in such exile and affliction?
q.w: Letter from exile in the Crimea to a beloved friend
q.o: Si enim peregrinos illic, id est, Romae, ita reficit sanctus Petrus, quid dicemus de nobis, qui proprii servi ejus sumus, et saltem ad momentum ministravimus ei, et in tali exsilio et afflictione consistimus?

q.t: It is ever our whole desire, by our letters, to console your charity and to relieve you of the anxiety you have about us; and with you, all the saints and our brethren who care for us for the Lord's sake.
q.w: Second letter from exile in the Crimea
q.o: Omne desiderium habemus semper litteris nostris charitatem vestram consolandi, et relevandi vos a sollicitudine quae vobis de nobis est: vobiscum vero et omnes sanctos et fratres nostros, qui curam nostri propter Dominum gerunt.

q.t: I have marveled, and I marvel still, at the thoughtlessness and want of compassion of all who once belonged to me, my friends and my kinsfolk, that they have so utterly forgotten my misfortune and, as I find, do not even wish to know whether I am still upon the earth or not.
q.w: Second letter from exile in the Crimea
q.o: Miratus sum autem, et adhuc miror indiscretionem et incompassionem omnium qui quondam mihi pertinebant, et amicorum meorum ac propinquorum, quia sic funditus infelicitatis meae obliti sunt, et nec scire volunt, ut invenio, sive sim super terram, sive non sim.

q.t: Nevertheless, may God, who will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth, through the intercession of Saint Peter establish their hearts in the orthodox faith, strengthen them against every heretic and every person hostile to our Church, and keep them unshaken, above all the shepherd who is now shown to be set over them.
q.w: Second letter from exile in the Crimea
q.l: Epistle 17 (Cherson, 655), praying for the Roman clergy and the pastor who replaced him; Migne PL 87, col. 204B-C
q.o: Verumtamen Deus, qui omnes vult salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire, per intercessiones sancti Petri stabiliat corda eorum in orthodoxa fide, et confirmet contra omnem haereticum et adversariam Ecclesiae nostrae personam, et immobiles custodiat, praecipue pastorem qui eis nunc praeesse monstratur

q.t: As for this lowly body of mine, the Lord himself will take care of it, governing it as it pleases him, whether in unceasing tribulations or in some small relief. For the Lord is nigh, and why am I anxious? For I hope in his mercies that he will not delay to finish my course in the way he has ordained.
q.w: Second letter from exile in the Crimea
q.o: De humili namque hoc corpore meo et ipsi Domino cura erit, ut sibi gubernare placet, sive in tribulationibus indesinentibus, sive in modico refrigerio. Dominus enim prope est, et quid sollicitus sum? Spero quippe in miserationes ejus, quod non tardet modo finire meum quo jusserit cursum.

q.t: Greet all your household for the Lord's sake, and all who for the love of God have shared the sufferings of my chains. May God most high protect you with his mighty hand from every temptation, and save you into his kingdom.
q.w: Second letter from exile in the Crimea
q.o: Omnes vestrates propter Dominum salutate, et omnes qui pro Dei amore meis compassi sunt vinculis. Deus excelsus potenti manu sua protegat vos ab omni tentatione, et salvet in regnum suum.

q.t: What remained was, that the people should be informed of all this proceeding, that they might see those very men established in the Church whom they had long seen and mourned as wanderers and scattered.
q.w: Letter to Cyprian on the return of the confessors to unity
q.l: Cyprian, Epistle 45 (Oxford ed. 49), §2, Cornelius to Cyprian (A.D. 251); ANF vol. 5

q.t: Their will being known, a great concourse of the brotherhood was assembled. There was one voice from all, giving thanks to God; all were expressing the joy of their heart by tears, embracing them as if they had this day been set free from the penalty of the dungeon.
q.w: Letter to Cyprian on the return of the confessors to unity
q.l: Cyprian, Epistle 45 (Oxford ed. 49), §2, Cornelius to Cyprian (A.D. 251); ANF vol. 5

q.t: Wherefore we bade Maximus the presbyter to take his own place; the rest we received with great approbation of the people. But we remitted all things to Almighty God, in whose power all things are reserved.
q.w: Letter to Cyprian on the return of the confessors to unity
q.l: Cyprian, Epistle 45 (Oxford ed. 49), §2, Cornelius to Cyprian (A.D. 251); ANF vol. 5

q.t: But we believe--nay, we confide in it for certain--that the others also who have been ranged in this error will shortly return into the Church when they see their leaders acting with us.
q.w: Letter to Cyprian on the return of the confessors to unity
q.l: Cyprian, Epistle 45 (Oxford ed. 49), §3, Cornelius to Cyprian (A.D. 251); ANF vol. 5

q.t: One of these bishops shortly after came back to the church, lamenting and confessing his transgression. And we communed with him as with a layman, all the people present interceding for him.
q.l: As quoted by Eusebius, Church History 6.43.10; NPNF 2nd ser. vol. 1

q.t: This avenger of the Gospel then did not know that there should be one bishop in a catholic church; yet he was not ignorant (for how could he be?) that in it there were forty-six presbyters, seven deacons, seven sub-deacons, forty-two acolyths, fifty-two exorcists, readers, and janitors, and over fifteen hundred widows and persons in distress, all of whom the grace and kindness of the Master nourish.
q.l: As quoted by Eusebius, Church History 6.43.11; NPNF 2nd ser. vol. 1 (on Novatian and the Roman church)

q.t: Whatever, my lord emperor, shall seem just and pleasing to the Lord when I have come into your presence, that I promise to do.
q.l: Epistle 1, written on being summoned to the Council of Milan (355); Migne PL 12, col. 947C-D
q.o: Quidquid, domine imperator, cum in praesentiam venero, justum fuerit visum et Domino placitum, id me facturum promitto.

q.t: So I learned, dearest brethren, that you were safe, as I had longed to hear. And as though I had suddenly been carried across the whole distance of the lands (as happened to Habacuc, who was carried by an angel all the way to Daniel), so I felt that I had come to you, as I received each one's letter and read in your writings of your holy friends and of your love.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.l: Epistle 2, §1 (from exile at Scythopolis); Migne PL 12, col. 948D-949A
q.o: Agnovi itaque, fratres charissimi, vos, ut desiderabam, esse incolumes. Et quasi subito raptum omni longinquitate terrarum (ut Habacuc factum est, qui per angelum portatus fuit usque ad Danielem) sic me judicavi ad vos pervenisse, dum singulorum litteras accipio, dumque sanctos amicos vestros et amorem in scriptis vestris percurro.

q.t: Tears were mingled with my joy, and my mind, eager to read on, was held back by the work of weeping.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Miscebantur mihi cum gaudio lacrymae: et avidus ad legendum animus occupatione lacrymarum tenebatur.

q.t: So for days, busied in this way and feeling that I was serving together with you, I forgot my past labors; for joys surrounded me on every side, offering here a steadfast faith, here love, here fruit; so that, set amid so many and such great blessings, I suddenly felt, as I said above, that I was not in exile but with you.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Sic per dies in occupatione hac vobiscum me famulari judicans, praeteritos labores obliviscebar: ita enim undique circumdabant me gaudia, hinc stabilem fidem, hinc dilectionem, hinc fructum porrigentia; ut in tot et tantis constitutus bonis, subito me, ut superius dixi, non in exsilio, sed vobiscum esse judicarem.

q.t: I rejoice, then, dearest brethren, in your faith; I rejoice in the salvation that follows faith; I rejoice in your fruits, for you reach out not only there where you are, but far away as well.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Gaudeo itaque, fratres charissimi, de fide vestra: gaudeo de salute quae fidem sequitur: gaudeo de fructibus, quod non solum illic constituti, sed et longe pergitis.

q.t: For as a farmer serves a good tree, which for the sake of its fruit does not suffer the axe and is not given over to the fire, so we too wish and long not only to render your holiness service according to the flesh, but to spend our very souls for your salvation.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Ut enim agricola arbori bonae inseruit illi, quae fructuum causa non securim patitur, non ignibus mancipatur; ita et nos vestrae sanctitati non solum servitium secundum carnem volumus et cupimus exhibere, sed animas nostras pro vestra salute impendere.

q.t: You have stretched out, as I said, strong and fruitful branches, and have labored to reach me across such vast stretches of land. I, the farmer, rejoice, and gladly gather the fruits of your labor, because you have been willing to do so much.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Extendistis, ut dixi, firmos cum fructu ramos, et per tam longa terrarum spatia ad me pertingere laborastis. Gaudeo agricola, et libens vestri laboris poma decerpo, quia tantum facere voluistis

q.t: But since, according to the divine commandments, we wished to make for you heavenly fruits out of earthly ones, lasting out of perishable, everlasting out of frail, we began to sow them every day among those who suffer want.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.l: Epistle 2, §2, on the gifts his people sent him; Migne PL 12, col. 949C
q.o: Sed cum nos secundum mandata divina, vobis volentes de terrenis coelestes, de caducis stabiles, de fragilibus sempiternos fructus facere; coepimus per necessitatem patientes quotidie seminare.

q.t: Therefore I leave my cause to God, that it may come to whatever end he himself shall ordain.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.l: Epistle 2, §4, from his written protest to his jailer Patrophilus; Migne PL 12, col. 950C
q.o: Ideo Deo causam reservo, ut quemadmodum ipse ordinaverit, finem possit accipere.

q.t: Meanwhile they saw how the people welcomed us with joy as we returned. They surrounded our lodging with lamps. By the Lord's favor we began once more to minister to those in need.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Viderunt interea, quemadmodum nos revertentes populi cum gaudio susceperunt. Lucernis nostrum hospitium circumdederunt. Coepimus annuente Domino iterum egentibus ministrare.

q.t: I will begin with the bishops: some, while they fear to lose their rank, have lost the faith; and while they refuse to lose their earthly wealth and privileges, have counted heavenly treasures and true security as nothing. Led in the same way, the rest, seeing the bishops afraid of losing these things, have begun to love what they cannot keep forever.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Ab episcopis incipiam: dum honorem quidam timent amittere, ipsos fidem perdidisse; dumque facultates terrenas et immunitates nolunt perdere, coelestes thesauros et veram securitatem nullam judicasse. Sic quoque ducti caeteri, dum episcopos haec timentes perdere vident, amare coeperunt quae semper habere non possunt.

q.t: But let human fear depart from your hearts, most holy brethren, since you have the consolation of the Lord, who says: Fear ye not them that kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul. It is a time of testing: it is the time for the tried to be made known openly.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Sed recedat, sanctissimi, humanus timor a vestris animis, cum habeatis Domini consolationem, qui dicit: Nolite timere illos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem occidere non possunt. Tempus est probationis: tempus est, ut probati innotescant manifesti.

q.t: Therefore I earnestly beg you to guard the faith with all vigilance, to keep concord, to devote yourselves to prayer, and to remember us without ceasing, so that the Lord may deign to set free his Church, which is suffering throughout the whole world, and that we who are oppressed may be set free and rejoice with you.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.o: Propter quod satis vos peto, ut cum omni vigilantia custodiatis fidem, servetis concordiam, orationibus incumbatis, nostri memores sine intermissione sitis: ut dignetur Dominus Ecclesiam suam liberare quae super universum orbem laborat, et ut nos qui deprimimur, possimus vobiscum liberati gaudere

q.t: May the Godhead protect you, and make you live and flourish both here and in the world to come, with all who are yours, dearest and most deeply longed-for brethren.
q.w: Letter from exile to the clergy and people of Vercelli, Novara, Ivrea and Tortona
q.l: Epistle 2, §11, closing blessing; Migne PL 12, col. 954A-B
q.o: Divinitas vos protegat, florentesque vivere et hic et in futuro faciat cum omnibus vestris, fratres charissimi et satis desideratissimi.

q.t: We too, following in the footsteps of those predecessors, and seeing this Church militant, entrusted to us by God, tossed in these times by so many heresies, and so cruelly harassed and afflicted by so many wars and by the depraved morals of men, lift up our eyes, weeping but full of hope, to that mountain from which all help comes.
q.w: Consueverunt Romani Pontifices (bull on the Rosary)
q.l: Bull of 17 September 1569, §1 (Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. VII, 1862, const. CXXXIX)
q.o: Nos quoque, illorum praedecessorum vestigia sequentes, militantem hanc Ecclesiam divinitus nobis commissam, his temporibus tot haeresibus agitatam, tot bellis pravisque hominum moribus atrociter vexatam et afflictam cernentes, lacrymabundos, sed spei plenos, oculos in montem illum, unde omne auxilium provenit, levamus
q.oe: Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. 7 (1862); Laderchi, Annales ecclesiastici 35 (1880)

q.t: And when this manner of praying had been spread abroad by the followers of Blessed Dominic, that is, by the friars of the said Order, and had been taken up by some, the faithful, kindled by these meditations and inflamed by these prayers, began suddenly to be changed into other men.
q.w: Consueverunt Romani Pontifices (bull on the Rosary)
q.l: Bull of 17 September 1569, prologue, on the Rosary preached by St Dominic (Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. VII, 1862, const. CXXXIX)
q.o: orandique modo praedicto per asseclas B. Dominici , fratres videlicet Ordinis praedicti, divulgato et a nonnullis accepto, coeperunt christifideles his meditationibus accensi, his precibus inflammati, in alios viros repente mutari
q.oe: Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. 7 (1862); Laderchi, Annales ecclesiastici 35 (1880)

q.t: God is wonderful in his saints. By the mouth of the prophet he promised to give them unto praise and glory and honour, so that those whom he crowns from heaven for the merits of their holiness, shining like the sun in his sight, he might also wonderfully honour in this world; and that in the office of praise and veneration which he commands to be paid to them he might recognize the honour and glory due also to his own Majesty.
q.w: Mirabilis Deus (bull declaring St Thomas Aquinas a Doctor of the Church)
q.l: Bull of 11 April 1567, prologue (Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. VII, p. 564; text as reprinted in Mühlbauer…)
q.o: Mirabilis Deus in sanctis suis, qui se daturum illos in laudem et gloriam et honorem, prophetae ore, promisit, ut quos, sicut sol in conspectu suo fulgentes, ob merita sanctitatis coronat de coelo, admirabiliter etiam honoraret in saeculo, et in eo, quod illis tribui jubet, laudis et venerationis officio, debitum quoque Majestati suae honorem et gloriam agnosceret.
q.oe: Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. 7 (1862); Laderchi, Annales ecclesiastici 35 (1880)

q.t: Before God and our Lord Jesus Christ we adjure you, brother, to defend and protect with all diligence the Gentiles converted to the Christian faith from the soldiers' injuries, and earnestly to admonish and exhort your suffragans, in our name too, to do the same. For it is to be feared that through such scandals God's name may be blasphemed among the Gentiles, and fewer embrace the Christian faith, offended by the sins of Christians and deterred by their injuries.
q.w: Letter to Alonso de Montúfar, Archbishop of Mexico
q.l: Brief of 7 October 1567 (Goubau, Epistolae, I.19), as printed in Laderchi, Annales ecclesiastici, vol. 35…
q.o: fraternitatem tuam coram Deo et Domino nostro Jesu Christo obtestamur, ut Gentiles ad fidem Christianam conversos, a militum injuriis quam diligentissime defendas ac protegas, et suffraganeos tuos, nostro etiam nomine, ut idem faciant, sedulo admoneas et horteris. Verendum est enim, ne propter talia scandala nomen Dei in gentibus blasphemetur , et minus multi Christianam fidem suscipiant, Christianorum peccatis offensi injuriisque deterriti.
q.oe: Bullarium Romanum, Turin ed., vol. 7 (1862); Laderchi, Annales ecclesiastici 35 (1880)

q.t: The life which we have received from God we ought to spend for God. I would quite willingly shed my blood for the love of God, and would give a thousand lives if I had them for Him and His faith. I feel quite jealous of those who shed their blood for Jesus Christ and for the Catholic faith.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 1, p. 221: a saying he often repeated (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: In the next life we must either enjoy an eternity of happiness, or suffer an eternity of woe.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 2, p. 235: a saying he repeated very often (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: As food gratifies the palate, and feeds and strengthens the limbs, so, hearing God spoken of, gives a wonderful gratification and vigour to the spirit.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 3, p. 243: on the profit he drew from sermons (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Would to God that in the hour of my death one sigh or one blessing of these poor creatures may fall upon me!
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 4, p. 249: a saying of his while serving the sick poor in the hospitals (as recorded in the…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: I do not think that there is a flower-bed in the world, whose scent would give me such pleasure as the smell of the hospital, which I feel quite refreshing.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 4, p. 258: his answer to one who asked how he could bear the smell of the hospital (as…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: My brother, charity seeks not its own convenience. Is not the sun also God's creature? My brother, we must give the spur to this jade of a body of ours, to make it trot on and get forwards.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 4, p. 258: to a friend who begged him not to cross to the hospital in the scorching sun (as…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: The good soldier dies in battle, the good sailor on the sea, and the good Minister of the Sick in the hospital.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 4, p. 259: to a priest who feared he would one day die among the sick (as recorded in the Life…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Do you want to know whether you are in conformity with the heart of God, and are walking in the way of perfection? Examine yourself, and see how you act with regard to the promise which you have made to God, and then if you find yourself warm in the ministry of our holy Institute, it is a good sign; but if you find yourself cold, it is a bad sign.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 4, p. 263: to one of his priests (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: If no poor could be found in the world, men ought to go in search of them, and dig them up from under ground to do them good, and to be merciful to them.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 10, p. 313 (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Patch upon patch; it is not the pretty dress, but good works that make the good religious.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 11, p. 317: of his old, much-mended habit (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: These people boast of being religious, and of having made the vow of poverty; but they don't like to feel the weight of the inconveniences of poverty.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 11, p. 318: of religious anxious to obtain extra garments (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Woe to us sinners, if we had not in heaven this great advocate, the treasurer of all the graces that come from the hand of God.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 17, p. 383: of the Blessed Virgin, whose rosary he said every night (as recorded in the Life…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Ah, mother of mercy, by the constancy that thou didst show when thou stoodest under the cross and saw thy Son crucified and dead, procure for me the grace to save my soul.
q.l: Vol. I, Book II, ch. 20, p. 209: to Our Lady in a picture of the Crucifixion, in his last days, Rome 1614 (as…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: My brothers, when you are praying, if you feel any devotion or spiritual consolation, thank God for it. If not, do not be discouraged, but think always, that for some defect or other you have not deserved it.
q.l: Vol. I, Book III, ch. 17, p. 375: advice to the lay-brothers on prayer (as recorded in the Life by Sanzio Cicatelli and Pantaleone Dolera)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Ah, Signor Galliani, there is another doctor waiting for me.
q.l: Vol. I, Book II, ch. 20, p. 211: to his physician, shortly before his death in 1614 (as recorded in the Life by…)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: I receive every day Him who came ' to bring fire and a sword,' and yet I am cold and idle, and still cling to earthly affections. I have the boldness to offer Him, from whom the sun itself receives its light, and who has created the whole world! What wonderful love to be chosen a minister to such a God! Oh! pray for me that my icy soul may become a fiery furnace.
q.l: Written from Rome to the Augustinian nun Laura Mignani of Brescia

q.t: I believe my heart must be as hard as a diamond not to have melted at such a moment!
q.l: Same letter, after describing how Our Lady placed the Christ Child in his arms at St Mary Major; Herbert (1873), p. 19

q.t: I shall never cease to give all I can to the poor and suffering, until the time comes when I shall be so despoiled of my goods that I shall have to be buried by charity.
q.l: His answer to John Dominic Zaninelli, rector of the Congregation of St Jerome at Vicenza, who warned him he was…

q.t: We may possess our Lord Jesus Christ, and we will not! Woe to that soul who can be thus indifferent to receive her God and Saviour!
q.w: Letter to his niece Elisabetta Porto
q.l: Written to his niece, Countess Elizabeth of Thiene, wife of Count Porto, soon after her marriage in 1521, urging frequent Communion

q.t: I have only one wish and that is to do the will of God in whatever place or way He may appoint. I feel that He demands of me a complete sacrifice of myself, and I am willing to obey.

Humility is a better passport for admission among us than temporal goods or great talents. We do not despise learning; but we care more that those who embrace our rule should be animated with the spirit of God. 'Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.'
q.l: To a gentleman of high birth and talent who offered to enter the Theatines on his own conditions; Herbert (1873), p. 36

q.t: Holy Father, it were better for us to die on the road than to hesitate a single day in obeying your commands.
q.l: His reply to the Pope (Clement VII), who asked why he set out for Naples in the heat of the dog-days, 1533

q.t: I believe that the God of Venice is equally the God of Naples
q.l: To those who objected, when he refused fixed revenues for his community at Naples, that Naples was not so rich as Venice

q.t: When my Lord and Saviour died on a Cross, I will only die on ashes.
