q.l: Refusing a softer mattress in his last illness, Naples, August 1547; Herbert (1873), p. 46

q.t: I do not know, my dear brethren, that I have ever offended any one of you intentionally; at least, I do not remember having done so; but if I have ever given pain to any one I now most humbly beg his pardon.
q.l: To his religious gathered at his deathbed, Naples, 1547; Herbert (1873), p. 46

q.t: If I have lived as a poor man, and if I am now dying, by my own wish, in extreme poverty, it is because I have always so highly esteemed that virtue. I earnestly commend the love and practice of holy poverty to you all.
q.l: To his religious at his deathbed, Naples, 1547; Herbert (1873), p. 47

q.t: It would be much better for me, my dear mother, to be blind all the rest of my life, than to be obliged to see the vanities and follies of the world.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. II, p. 11 (1847 ed.); her answer to her mother, as recorded by her biographers (Hansen, via Feuillet)
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: As I cannot do any good, is it not just that I should suffer whatever I am capable of enduring?
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. V, p. 37 (1847 ed.); her reply to those urging her to moderate her austerities, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Lord, may Thy will be done, not mine; I abandon myself to Thy Divine dispensations.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. X, p. 66 (1847 ed.); her prayer in times of interior desolation, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Oh how advantageous and agreeable it would be to be always ill and to suffer great pains, if we did not give so much trouble to those who attend upon us!
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XII, p. 84 (1847 ed.); a saying she often repeated, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Oh, my Jesus! oh, my Jesus! increase my sufferings, but increase also Thy Divine love in my soul!
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XII (1847 ed. p. 86-87); text from the Kenedy reprint, p. 127
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Oh my God! who would not love Thee? Oh good Jesus! when shall I begin to love Thee as I am obliged? How far am I from this perfect, intimate, and generous love? Alas! I know not even how to love thee. How shameful! What advantage is it to have a heart, unless it be quite consumed with the love of Thee!
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XIII (1847 ed. p. 88-89); text from the Kenedy reprint, p. 130
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Lord Jesus Christ, God and Man, my Creator and my Saviour, I am extremely sorry and sensibly grieved for having offended Thee, because Thou art what Thou art, and because I love Thee above all things.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XIII, p. 89 (1847 ed.); opening of an ejaculatory prayer she composed
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Oh, Salvation of my soul! I desire to love Thee as Thou lovest Thyself. Oh, my most sweet Jesus! may I burn with the fire of Thy divine love; may it consume me, and make of my soul a holocaust to Thy glory.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XIII, p. 89 (1847 ed.); close of the same prayer she composed
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Let us love God, let us love Him with all our hearts.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XIII, p. 90 (1847 ed.); the words with which she always began her conversations, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: May God be eternally glorified, and His most pure Mother, the Virgin Mary, honoured by every creature! I have made this spiritual garment, and have acquitted myself of this devotion, by the help of the grace of my God, who has supplied for my defects.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XV, p. 110 (1847 ed.); written in her own hand after her 'spiritual garment' of prayers and fasts for Our Lady
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Ah, if it were permitted to me to exercise the function of preacher, I would go by day and by night barefoot into the most public places, covered with a hair-shirt, and bearing a large cross on my shoulders, to exhort sinners to do penance, and to represent to them the fearful severity of the judgments of God.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XVI, p. 115 (1847 ed.); words she sometimes uttered out of zeal for sinners, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: O father, what great things I could tell you of the pleasures and abundant consolations which God will bestow upon His saints for all eternity! I go with inconceivable satisfaction to contemplate the adorable Face of God, whom I have all my life desired to possess.
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XIX, p. 145 (1847 ed.); to Fr. Francis Nieto, two hours before her death, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: Jesus, be with me; Jesus, be with me
q.w: The Life of St. Rose of Lima
q.l: Ch. XIX, p. 146 (1847 ed.); her last words, 24 August 1617, as recorded by her biographers
q.tr: Oratorian series, ed. F. W. Faber

q.t: I have no choice but the good pleasure of God. Be it done unto me according to His will. For my own part, I would prefer to die, and for my soul to fly to Him at once; but I accept all at His hands, be it life or be it death.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. II; her answer during her grave illness in youth, as recorded by her early biographers (Mattiotti and the process)

q.t: His brow is always serene; his glances kindle in the soul the flame of ardent devotion. When I look upon him, I understand the glory of the angelic nature, and the degraded condition of our own.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. VII; describing her guardian archangel at the order of her director Don Antonio, as recorded by Mattiotti

q.t: Be not afraid, father; the archangel will not allow me to proceed too far in that course. He always checks me when I am tempted to transgress the bounds of prudence.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. VII; to her director Don Antonio when he hesitated over her penances, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: Hope every thing from the mercy of God; it is as boundless as His power.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. IX; to the parents of the mute child Camilla, as recorded in the canonization testimony

q.t: The Blessed Virgin requires at our hands more fervent prayers, more tears, more penances. We must supply for the great dearth of love.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XII; exhortation to her Oblates in a time of disorder in Rome, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: We are few; but do not doubt the strength of prayer. Let us be fervent and persevere, and soon we shall reap the fruit of our intense supplications, of our long-continued pleadings; and liberty, peace, and all God's blessings, will be restored to Rome.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XII; the same exhortation to her Oblates, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: Lord Jesus, I have been thoughtless in bringing my sisters here, and forgetting to provide food for them. Help us in our need.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIII; her prayer in the vineyard when the sisters were hungry and thirsty, as recorded in the canonization testimony

q.t: My child, you do not trust enough in God. Look up and see.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIII; to the young Oblate Perna, as recorded in the canonization testimony

q.t: Dear sister, give up the love and the vanities of the world, and God will take pity upon you.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIII; to Palozza Altieri, whose husband was dying, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: Be Thou eternally praised and blessed, O my dear Lord Jesus Christ! Thanks be to Thee for the unmerited favours I have received at Thy hands. To Thee, to Thee alone, do I owe all the blessings I have, and have yet to receive.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIV; heard by Sister Augustina during her last illness, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: God be praised, my pilgrimage will end from Wednesday to Thursday next.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIV; to those who hoped she would recover, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: I see them no more. God has conquered; His foes have fled.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIV; to her confessor Don Giovanni (Mattiotti), asked whether the evil spirits still troubled her, as recorded…

q.t: God's will is my will; His good pleasure mine. If He Chooses me to tarry yet on earth, so be it then. I am ready to remain in this miserable world, if He commands it.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIV; to her Oblates, who begged her to ask God to let her live, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: Satan will assault you, as he has assaulted me; but be not afraid. You will overcome him through patience and obedience; and no trial will be too grievous, if you are united to Jesus; if you walk in His ways, He will be with you.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIV; her last instructions to her Oblates, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: The heavens open! The angels descend! The archangel has finished his task. He stands before me. He beckons to me to follow him.
q.w: The Life of St. Frances of Rome
q.l: Ch. XIV; her last words, 9 March 1440, to her confessor, as recorded by her biographers

q.t: I must make Jesus willingly possessor of my heart, since reason instals Him as King of it.
q.w: Notes of her retreats (in Lady Lovat's Life)
q.l: Ch. II, p. 28; from her own retreat notes

q.t: I have desired to have no existence of my own, having been so constantly sustained by God's grace it seems to me all I am, or have, is due to Him.
q.w: Notes of her retreats (in Lady Lovat's Life)
q.l: Ch. II, p. 28; from her own retreat notes

q.t: In imitation of our Blessed Lady I wish to dedicate myself to God for the service of my neighbour in a manner which will subject me to blame in the eyes of the world, thus imitating our Lord Who throughout His life despised all such considerations for the good of His creatures. All that I wish is to accomplish His divine Will.
q.w: Notes of her retreats (in Lady Lovat's Life)
q.l: Ch. II, p. 28; a resolution from her scattered notes

q.t: You console me greatly by the news you give of our poor Sister. I cannot doubt that God will bless His work as long as we act with confidence in Him and dependence on His Divine Will.
q.l: P. 175; letter to the Abbé de Vaux, 6 May 1640

q.t: We should consider the interests of those with whom we work more than we should our own, or even those of the company. This is what has been taught to us by our very revered Father who has learned it from the Son of God, Jesus crucified.
q.l: P. 257; letter to Sister Jeanne at Montreuil

q.t: Accept the order and leading of Divine Providence with entire submission. One day you and I shall be blessing God for these persecutions.
q.l: P. 275; letter to her Daughters in their trials

q.t: This life is short, and the reward of our sufferings is eternal; but it is only given to those who have behaved themselves valiantly. I wish you all victorious in this combat.
q.w: Sayings to the Sisters (in Lady Lovat's Life)
q.l: P. 312; spoken when announcing hardships to a community

q.t: We must submit to the ruling of Divine Providence, and attach ourselves the more strongly to God when suffering the privation of consolations from creatures.
q.l: P. 318; letter to a Sister Servant on confidence in God in trials

q.t: My dear Sisters, you have always told me that you had only one heart in your three persons. In the name of the Blessed Trinity whom you desire to honour I beg of you to enlarge it so as to make room for our three Sisters to enter into this cordial union, so that there should not be any distinction between the three first and the three last.
q.l: P. 345; letter to the Sisters in Warsaw, 19 August

q.t: My Sisters, have you ever noticed how masons make use of a level to rectify their work, not thinking it safe to trust to their eye? Well, my dear Sisters, the conference is our level which we then pass up and down on our conduct, by which we can judge of its defects.
q.w: Conferences to the Sisters (in Lady Lovat's Life)
q.l: P. 383; on the use of the community conferences

q.t: Do you remember to say the prayer for the sick morning and evening, and the Benedicite and grace at meals? Do you take napkins to their bedside, and see that they are always clean? But above all, my dear Sister, have you a great love for their salvation?
q.l: P. 397; letter to a Sister on the service of 'our masters the poor'

q.t: Courage then, my dear Sisters. Let us do all things joyfully with hearts filled with the love of God, Who can cause us to find roses even among thorns.
q.l: P. 397; letter to the Sisters working in a hospital

q.t: It has not pleased God as yet to blot me out from the face of the earth, though it is so long since I have deserved it. One must await the order of His Providence with submission.
q.l: P. 437; letter to a Sister, 10 June [1656], after a grave illness

q.t: Be very careful of your service of the poor; and above all to live together in great union and cordiality—loving one another in imitation of the union and life of our Saviour. I beg of you to take the Blessed Virgin as your only Mother.
q.w: Last words to her Daughters (in Lady Lovat's Life)
q.l: P. 453; her last blessing to the Sisters of Charity on her deathbed (March 1660), as recorded by those present

q.t: This is the way I shall go about when I am poor and in misery for the love of God.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 186; trying on a poor grey cloak before her handmaids, as recorded by her handmaids (Libellus: 'Sic incedam…)

q.t: Yes, indeed, my Lord, if Thou wishest to be with me, I wish to be with Thee and never to be separated from Thee.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 282; spoken in ecstasy at Eisenach, as recorded by her handmaid Ysentrude (Libellus)

q.t: I saw the heavens open, and my Lord, the most merciful Jesus, deigned to look down upon me, and to console me in all the tribulations by which I am oppressed.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 282; explaining her ecstasy to Ysentrude, as recorded by her handmaid Ysentrude (Libellus: 'Vidi celum apertum...')

q.t: I thank Thee for having thus mercifully consoled my afflicted and desolate soul. He offered himself to Thee, and I too had offered him to Thee, for the defence of Thy Holy Land. I do not regret that sacrifice, though I loved him with all my heart.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 305; her prayer at Bamberg over the bones of her husband Louis, as recorded by her handmaids (Libellus: 'Domine, gratias ago tibi...')

q.t: I told you so indeed; we ought to make people as happy as possible.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 352; hearing the poor she had fed singing for joy, as recorded by her handmaids (Libellus: 'Ecce dixi vobis, quod…)

q.t: If we are wise, we shall imitate the snail, who, when it rains, withdraws into its shell; let us obey then, and retrace our steps.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 357; to Master Conrad's messenger, who recalled her from a journey, as recorded by her handmaids (Libellus)

q.t: I have no need of such an image, for I carry it in my heart.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 377; refusing a beautiful image offered to her, as recorded by her handmaids (Libellus: 'Non habeo opus tali…)

q.t: I will tell you; a charming little bird came and placed himself between me and the wall, and there he sang to me for a long time in such soft and sweet notes, and my heart and soul were so rejoiced, that I could not help singing myself.
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 383; a few days before her death, to her handmaid Elizabeth, as recorded by that handmaid (Libellus: 'inter me et…)

q.t: Let us speak of God and of the Infant Jesus; for this is midnight, the hour that Jesus was born, and was laid in the manger, and created a new star that none had ever seen before
q.w: Life of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary (Montalembert)
q.l: P. 387; on the night of her death, 16-17 November 1231, as recorded by her handmaids (Libellus: 'Modo loquamur de Deo et puero Jesu...')

q.t: And do not be troubled if deep recollection makes you pass for melancholy; people have almost always said that of me, and it was when my spirit was in very great jubilation with God. The truth is that the joys which come from God and those which spring from creatures are very different, and the world ordinarily sees only what belongs to the world.
q.l: Letter CXLIII, to her son, Quebec, 11 October 1659 (ed. Richaudeau, vol. II, p. 145)
q.o: Et ne vous mettez pas en peine si un grand recueillement vous fait passer pour mélancolique; l'on a presque toujours dit cela de moi, et c'était lorsque mon esprit était en de très-grandes jubilations avec Dieu. C'est que les joies qui viennent de Dieu et celles qui naissent des créatures sont bien différentes, et le monde ne voit ordinairement que ce qui est du monde.

q.t: How good it is, my dearest daughter, to love him, but to love him in the right way, that is, by dying to oneself a thousand times a day in a spirit of sacrifice.
q.l: Letter CL, to a young Ursuline, Quebec, 23 October 1660 (vol. II, p. 186)
q.o: Qu'il fait bon, ma très-chère fille, de l'aimer, mais de l'aimer de la bonne manière, c'est-à-dire en mourant à soi-même mille fois le jour en esprit de sacrifice.

q.t: Let our hearts, then, have no movement save by the spirit of this divine Master, who absolutely and without reserve wills to be the spirit of our spirit.
q.l: Letter CL, to a young Ursuline, Quebec, 23 October 1660 (vol. II, p. 186)
q.o: Que nos cœurs n'aient donc plus de mouvement que par l'esprit de ce divin Maître, qui absolument et sans réserve veut être l'esprit de notre esprit.

q.t: Through this divine Heart I adore you for all those who do not adore you; I love you for all those who do not love you; I acknowledge you for all the wilfully blind who in their contempt do not acknowledge you. Through this divine Heart I wish to fulfil the duty of all mortals.
q.l: Letter CLIII, to her son, Quebec, 16 September 1661 (vol. II, p. 198)
q.o: Par ce divin Cœur je vous adore pour tous ceux qui ne vous adorent pas; je vous aime pour tous ceux qui ne vous aiment pas; je vous reconnais pour tous les aveugles volontaires qui par mépris ne vous reconnaissent pas. Je veux par ce divin Cœur satisfaire au devoir de tous les mortels.

q.t: You had not yet seen the light of day when my ambition for you was that you should be a servant of Jesus Christ, wholly devoted to his divine counsels, at the cost of your life and of mine.
q.l: Letter CLIII, to her son, Quebec, 16 September 1661 (vol. II, p. 196)
q.o: Vous n'aviez pas encore vu le jour que mon ambition pour vous était que vous fussiez serviteur de Jésus-Christ, et tout dévoué à ses divins conseils, aux dépens de votre vie et de la mienne.

q.t: It is likely that we shall see each other in the other world rather than in this one. Yet God has ways unknown to us, above all in a country as unsettled and uncertain as this, where, humanly speaking, there is no more security than in the leaves of the trees when they are tossed by the wind.
q.l: Letter CLIII, to her son, Quebec, 16 September 1661 (vol. II, p. 196)
q.o: Il est à croire que nous nous verrons plutôt en l'autre monde qu'en celui-ci. Dieu néanmoins a des voies qui nous sont inconnues, surtout dans un pays flottant et incertain comme celui-ci, où naturellement parlant, il n'y a pas plus d'assurance qu'aux feuilles des arbres quand elles sont agitées par le vent.

q.t: Let us then carry your cross together, uniting it to that of our most adorable Jesus, who will sweeten its bitterness by the sweetness of his spirit.
q.l: Letter CXXVIII, to a lady friend, Quebec, 9 September 1655 (vol. II, p. 75)
q.o: Portons donc ensemble votre croix en l'unissant à celle de notre très-adorable Jésus, qui en adoucira les amertumes par la douceur de son esprit.

q.t: Meanwhile, my dear sister, let us love our divine Spouse while others do not love him. Let us hide ourselves in this living rock, in this poor dwelling pierced on every side by his divine wounds, and let us meet there together, so as to live no longer except by his divine life and his holy influences.
q.l: Letter CXXII, to a lady friend, Quebec, 13 August 1654 (vol. II, p. 55)
q.o: Cependant, ma chère sœur, aimons notre divin Epoux pendant que les autres ne l'aiment pas. Cachons-nous dans cette pierre vive, dans cette masure, trouée de toute parts par ses divines plaies, et trouvons-nous-y ensemble pour ne vivre plus que de sa vie divine et de ses influences saintes.

q.t: Ah, my dear sister, what a great thing is the salvation of souls, which cost all the blood of the Son of God!
q.l: Letter CXXIII, to one of her sisters, Quebec, 13 August 1654 (vol. II, p. 56)
q.o: Ah! ma chère sœur, que c'est une grande chose que le salut des âmes qui ont coûté tout le sang du Fils de Dieu!

q.t: My dearest son, God has immense goodness toward simple souls who trust in him.
q.l: Letter CXXX, to her son, Quebec, 2 October 1655 (vol. II, p. 80)
q.o: Mon très-cher fils, Dieu a des bontés immenses sur les âmes simples et qui se confient en Lui.

q.t: Are we not exceedingly happy to be among the number of his children, and in a state where it depends only on us to become cherished and magnificent temples in which the Holy Spirit will take his delight?
q.l: Letter CXLII, to an Ursuline nun, Quebec, 25 September 1659 (vol. II, p. 144)
q.o: Ne sommes-nous pas trop heureuses d'être du nombre de ses enfants, et en un état où il ne tiendra qu'à nous de devenir des temples chéris et magnifiques, où le Saint-Esprit prendra ses délices?

q.t: I long for rest, so that I may prepare myself for death. People laugh at me when I speak of it, because they see me act in our affairs like a person who loves action, I mean with gladness and without gloom. But they do not see the depths of my soul, which wills to love its only Good in all things.
q.l: Letter CXLVI, to her former superior at Tours (Mother Françoise de Saint-Bernard), Quebec, 23 September 1660 (vol. II, p. 176)
q.o: J'aspire au repos afin de me disposer à la mort. L'on se rit de moi quand j'en parle, parce qu'on me voit agir dans nos affaires comme une personne qui aime l'action, je veux dire avec allégresse et sans chagrin. Mais on ne voit pas mon fond, qui est de vouloir aimer partout son unique bien;

q.t: But in the end you will go one day to join him in the dwelling of the blessed, where you will speak to each other spirit to spirit and glorify God in a new way. Ah, my dear Mother, when shall we be in that place of happiness? When shall we embrace one another in the purity of the saints?
q.l: Letter CXLVII, to an Ursuline of Tours on the death of her uncle and spiritual father, Quebec, 28 September 1660 (vol. II, p. 177)
q.o: Mais enfin, vous irez un jour avec lui dans le séjour des bienheureux, où vous vous parlerez esprit à esprit, et y glorifierez Dieu d'une nouvelle manière. Ah! ma chère Mère, quand serons-nous dans ce lieu de bonheur? Quand nous embrasserons-nous dans la pureté des Saints?

q.t: And do not be astonished if you see faults in your actions; it is this state of union, to which the Spirit of God is calling you, that opens your eyes. The more light this Spirit gives you, the more impurities you will see in them.
q.l: Letter CLXI, to her son, Quebec, 18 October 1663 (vol. II, p. 257)
q.o: Et ne vous étonnez point si vous voyez des défauts dans vos actions; c'est cet état d'union où l'esprit de Dieu vous appelle qui vous ouvre les yeux. Plus cet esprit vous donnera de lumière, plus vous y verrez d'impuretés.

q.t: Do not think that in choosing the religious state I am guided only by my own will; I assure you that I do but follow the will of Divine Providence. I am not afraid that you will refuse me, since it is God who calls, and I am obliged to obey His call.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter V, to his parents, Braine-le-Comte, December 25, 1858 (p. 27)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: So, remembering that on the day of my profession I had already put myself under the funeral pall, I offered myself to his lordship to meet, if he thought it well, this second death.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XVII, to his brother Pamphile, Molokai, November 25, 1873 (pp. 91-92)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: As for me, I make myself a leper with the lepers, to gain all to Jesus Christ. That is why in preaching, I say, We lepers, not, My brethren, as in Europe.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XVII, to his brother Pamphile, Molokai, November 25, 1873 (pp. 93-94)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: But our good Master knows how to repay us. Or rather He has already repaid us. If our Lord were to ask me: Quando misi vos sine sacculo et pera et calceamentis, numquid aliquid defuit vobis?—"When I sent you without purse, or scrip, or shoes, was anything wanting to you?" I should certainly have to reply, Nihil, Domine.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XVII, to his brother Pamphile, Molokai, November 25, 1873 (p. 94)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: So I had to tramp as I was, over stones and ruts, through mud and rain, to my hut. Well, here I am again safe and sound, regretting indeed the probable loss of my cloak, but full of joy at having helped to save a soul. May the good Jesus be praised!
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XVIII, to his brother Pamphile, Molokai, December 8, 1874, after a night sick-call in the rain when his horse…
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: I want to be unknown to the world, and now I find, in consequence of the few letters I have written, that I am being talked about on all sides, even in America.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XX, to his mother and brothers, Kalawao, Molokai, March 15, 1876, annoyed that his letter had been printed (p. 110)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: Almighty God intends to teach you not to attach yourselves to the things of this world. Let us remember that it is a place of exile, and that those who die in the Lord are far happier than you or I who are left here below. Sometimes I am inclined to envy my poor sick Christians, when I administer the last sacraments to them and bury them.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XX, to his mother and brothers, Kalawao, Molokai, March 15, 1876, consoling his brother Gérard after a death in the family (p. 110)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: My greatest pleasure is to go there to say my beads, and meditate on that unending happiness which so many of them are already enjoying. There, too, my thoughts dwell on the sufferings of Purgatory. I confess to you, my dear brother, the cemetery and the hospital, where the dying lie, are my best meditation books, as well for the benefit of my own soul as in view of preparing my instructions.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XXIV, to his brother Pamphile, Kalawao, Molokai, January 31, 1880, of the cemetery beside his church (p. 118)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: I cannot come to Honolulu, for leprosy has attacked me. There are signs of it on my left cheek and ear, and my eyebrows are beginning to fall; I shall soon be quite disfigured. As I have no doubt of the real character of the malady, I remain calm, resigned, and very happy in the midst of my people. The good God knows what is best for my sanctification, and I say daily, Fiat voluntas tua, with a ready heart.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter to his bishop, Mgr. Koeckmann, 1885 (p. 133)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: I would not be cured, if the price of my cure was that I must leave the island, and give up my work.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Said to a visitor after he had contracted leprosy, as recorded by the editors (p. 134)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: As you know, a long time ago I myself have been chosen by Divine Providence as a victim to this loathsome disease. I hope to be eternally thankful to God for this favour; as it seems to me that this disease may shorten a little, and even make more direct, my road to our dear fatherland.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XXVIII, to his brother Pamphile, Molokai, November 9, 1887, written in English (pp. 141-142)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: Such being my hope, I have accepted this malady as my special cross, which I try to carry, as Simon the Cyrenian, in the footsteps of our Divine Master. Please help me with your good prayers to obtain persevering strength, till I happily arrive at the top of Calvary.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XXVIII, to his brother Pamphile, Molokai, November 9, 1887, written in English (p. 142)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: The joy and contentment of heart that the Sacred Hearts deluge me with, make me consider myself the happiest missioner in the world. Consequently the sacrifice of my health, which our good God has deigned to accept that He may render my ministry among the lepers more fruitful, appears after all but a slight affair, and even profitable for me.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XXVIII, to his brother Pamphile, postscript of November 16, 1887 (p. 143)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: I am still able, but not without some difficulty, to stand every day at the altar, where I do not forget any of you. Do you, in return, pray and get prayers for me, who am being gently drawn towards the grave. May God strengthen me, and give me the grace of perseverance and of a happy death.
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Letter XXIX, his last letter, to his brother Pamphile, February 19, 1889 (p. 146)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: Look at my eyes. I have seen so many lepers die, that I cannot be mistaken. Death is not far off. I should have liked to have seen the Bishop again, but the good God is calling me to celebrate Easter with Himself. May God be blessed for it!
q.w: Life and Letters of Father Damien
q.l: Words in his last days, Holy Week 1889, as recorded by Father Wendelin (Letter of Father Wendelin, p. 147)
q.tr: Catholic Truth Society, ed. Fr. Pamphile De Veuster

q.t: I do not know. These things go together and are not to be compared. What I do know is that I was happy on both occasions.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Asked whether her First Communion or her meetings with the Blessed Virgin at the grotto had made her happier, as…

q.t: My God, you have wished it. I accept the chalice you have given me. May your holy Name be blessed!
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: On the death of her mother during her novitiate at Nevers, as recorded in The Lily of Mary (p. 68)

q.t: What idea can you have of me? Do I not know that if the Blessed Virgin chose me it was because I was the most ignorant of all. If she had found another more ignorant than I am, she would have chosen her in my place.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Reply to a superior who asked whether she had felt any temptation to self-love, as recorded in The Lily of Mary (pp. 70-71)

q.t: You are right, and that is my life. The Blessed Virgin made use of me, then she placed me in a corner. That is my place. I am happy in it and there will I remain.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: To a companion in the infirmary, after asking her where a broom is put once it has been used ('In the corner, behind…)

q.t: Yes, O tender Mother, you have stooped even to earth, to a weak little child, to communicate to her certain things in spite of her unworthiness. And what reason had she not for humiliation? You, the Queen of heaven and earth, made use of what, according to the world, was the weakest of things.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Her written prayer to the Blessed Virgin, May 12, 1866 (p. 72)

q.t: I place my joy in being a victim of the heart of Jesus; union, intimate union with Him, such as St. John had, by purity and love.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: As recorded in The Lily of Mary, ch. 'Fragrance of the Hidden Life' (p. 75)

q.t: My soul is filled with strength and confidence in thinking that it is not I who pray, but Jesus in me.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Letter to the Mother General, then at Rome, about her Communion days (p. 78)

q.t: After the example of Jesus, and for the love of Jesus, I will carry the cross hidden in my heart with courage and generosity. For the love of our Lord, I will generously accept privations, sufferings and humiliations, as did Jesus and Mary, to glorify God.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)

q.t: O Jesus, give me, I pray Thee, the bread of patience to bear the trials which I suffer. O Jesus, Thou wishest me to be crucified: Fiat.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)

q.t: If people only knew how good she is! Say your rosary well; put yourself under her protection; you will never do so in vain.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Of the Blessed Virgin, a frequent saying, as recorded in The Lily of Mary (p. 81)

q.t: She is so beautiful, that when any one has seen her once he would die to see her again.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Of the Blessed Virgin, as recorded in The Lily of Mary (p. 82)

q.t: What folly to recoil when our Lord desires to nail our hands to the cross. The more I am crucified, the more I will rejoice.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: In interior suffering, as recorded in The Lily of Mary (pp. 85-86)

q.t: My soul rejoices to have one trait of likeness to Jesus—to remain hidden in helplessness.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Written during her long illness at Nevers (p. 86)

q.t: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for me, a poor sinner—a poor sinner.
q.w: The Lily of Mary (sayings and writings of Bernadette)
q.l: Her last words, Nevers, April 16, 1879, as recorded in The Lily of Mary (p. 87)

q.t: If we reflect well, for us there are no distances: the Missionaries of the Sacred Heart of Jesus must participate in the immensity of this Divine Heart, Who embraces all, comprehends all, animates all, unites all in Himself.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.l: Second Voyage to New York, letter of April 18, 1890 (p. 1)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: How many beautiful thoughts the calmness of the sea suggests. We see in it the happiness of a soul that lives in the tranquillity of the grace of God. In such a fortunate soul all is calm; peace undisturbed; it has the capacity of raising itself to the sublimity of the Divine mysteries.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.l: Second Voyage to New York, April 20, 1890 (p. 4)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: The soul full of earthly ties, full of attachments, is always narrow, very small, understands little, pusillanimous, frequently dejected, and is never able to throw itself into the immensity of Divine Service. I don't want any such souls among my daughters, nor among my friends. I want you all to have wings and fly swiftly and repose in that blessed peace possessed by a soul that is all for God.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.l: Second Voyage to New York, April 20, 1890 (p. 5)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Oh, happy the soul that lives in the true love of Christ! My daughters, detach yourselves from all persons and all things, and you will have a foretaste of the Paradise of true, solid and Heavenly love.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.l: Second Voyage to New York, April 1890 (p. 10)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: If you love God, come forth, have courage, the devil laughs at the weak, at the timid, whereas he fears and flies from energetic souls. Are you fearful? She who trusts in God and mistrusts herself, need fear nothing, because stripped of herself and strong with the strength of God, and with faith and humility, she can defy everything.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Mary is your Mother, Mistress and Foundress, obey and fulfil her desires. Mary speaks to you plainly; listen to her, trust her with all your affections, she will alienate them from creatures, and you, as angelic spirits, will take refuge in the Heart of Jesus. Offer yourselves often to Mary, pray, work, suffer, recreate yourselves, rest and walk with Mary and beneath the gaze of Mary, and never sadden her in the least.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Know, children, the Sacred Heart wants all or nothing. He wants no divided heart, no divisions. Woe to us if we have anxious affections for creatures or for ourselves. All must be placed in the Most Holy Heart of Jesus, all without reserve.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: The conversion of sinners and the sanctification of souls does not depend on sterile cold human eloquence, or the grace of style and flowery rhetoric, but on the fructifying grace of Jesus Christ. Jesus alone can give life to words and arguments. He enlightens the mind, moves the will, sows virtue, and animates us to undertake holy and perfect works.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: He marks in the book of life all the trials, troubles and crosses that we suffer for the salvation and sanctification of souls. He enumerates the days, hours and moments that we spend in this holy exercise, and all will be fully rewarded by the sovereign goodness of the Most Holy Heart of Jesus. Even a charitable word spoken will be amply remunerated because everything done for Jesus and with Jesus is great.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: In the secrecy of the Holy Tabernacle the loving Heart of Jesus takes note of our needs in order to help us, and waits for nothing more than to see us at His feet, full of confidence, uniting our prayers with His.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.l: New Orleans to Panama, 1895, for the month of the Sacred Heart (p. 93)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: In the meantime, make use of prayer, work with prayer. Have confidence in our Beloved Jesus, and always abandon yourselves to His Adorable Sacred Heart, and have hope, ever mistrusting yourselves and confiding in Him alone. For however weak and insignificant you are, you can surely do great things. "Omnia possum in Eo qui me confortat."
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Yes, my children, God is the beginning, the centre and the end of all our daily actions, and whilst as Missionaries of His Divine Heart we give great and continual glory to God, we also acquire for ourselves at every moment immense treasures of grace. Whether we work, eat, teach or sleep, or voyage, let us do all in the name of Jesus and in that of His Divine Heart.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.l: Liverpool to New York, November 1898, on the annual retreat (p. 166)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Let us frequently consider the graces with which we are continually surrounded through the immense goodness of God. Let it be an incentive to warm our hearts with holy gratitude, which in turn will inebriate us little by little with Divine Love.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters to her daughters)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: In great success, pray, and you will take your success moderately, for pride comes before a fall. In defeat, pray also, and trust will return and you will become strong with the strength of God.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters)
q.l: Letter to the Alumnae of Rome, May 1904 (p. 248)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Pray for yourselves, for those entrusted to your care, for the world, for the Church. Make a practice of prayer, and if you reach that degree of sweetness of prayer which is found in intimate converse with God, you will never have discomfort or despair. Dark clouds will not trouble for long the serenity of your souls.
q.w: Travels of Mother Frances Xavier Cabrini (letters)
q.l: Letter to the Alumnae of Rome, May 1904 (p. 248)
q.tr: anonymous (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)

q.t: Am I not more than ever the child of Providence? Did you not yourself give me up to God? He who watches over the birds of the air and the flowers of the field, will He not take care of me wherever I may be? I cannot help longing for you, and missing you terribly sometimes; but love suffers and is resigned, and the thoughts of Heaven grow more vivid as we become more detached from all on earth.
q.l: Letter to his father from the Foreign Mission Seminary, Paris, 1851 (ch. V, p. 48)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: Only a little more trust! A little more confidence in God! A little more patience! and the end will come, and the past weary years will seem as nothing; then will arrive the moment of reunion, and all will be amply compensated for and repaid, principal and interest. O Christian hope! How beautiful thou art!
q.l: Letter to his father from the Foreign Mission Seminary, Paris, 1851 (ch. V, p. 48)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: Let Mary always be your refuge, my darling brother. The Blessed Virgin is much loved and honored in the Mission House here. When you have any little sorrow or trouble go simply to her, and ask her to offer it up for you to our dear Lord, and there leave it without any further care or preoccupation. Then you will have nothing to fear either from men or devils.
q.l: Letter to his young brother Eusebius, Paris, 1851 (ch. V, p. 50)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: On Sunday evening next we go into retreat till the Saturday following, a holy and happy time of meditation and prayer, when we dwell under the shadow of the altar, free from cares and distractions, absorbed in God.
q.l: Letter written before the retreat preceding his ordination as deacon, Paris, December 1851 (ch. V, p. 52)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: I knew none of them; but my heart went out to them with love and sympathy, for are we not children of the same Father, servants of the same Master, soldiers of the same King? The same object unites us; the same grace, in different degrees, was distributed to us; the same God gave Himself to us; and we invoked the same Queen, Mary, Mother of the Saviour of the world.
q.l: Letter on his ordination as deacon beside men of many orders and nations, Paris, 1851 (ch. V, p. 53)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: I am now only waiting patiently for the day when God will allow me to offer Him the sacrifice of my blood. I do not regret leaving this world; my soul thirsts for the waters of eternal life. My exile is over. I touch the soil of my real country; earth vanishes, Heaven opens, I go to God.
q.l: Letter to his father, sister and brothers, from his cage at Kecho, Tong-king, January 2, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 182)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: My heart is as tranquil as a lake which reflects the blue sky and I have no fear. The mandarin of Nam-Xang, who spends his life tormenting the Christians, came to see me the other day, and I told him that "Jesus was stronger than he; that it was in vain he struggled with our Lord, and that he would have to yield to His power in the end."
q.l: Letter from his cage to Bishop Theurel, December 28, 1860 (ch. XIV, p. 184)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: I do so love this Tong-king mission! But now, in place of the sweat of my brow, I give it my blood. The sword hangs over my head but I have no fears. Our good God has taken pity on my weakness and filled me with Himself so that I am happy, and even joyous.
q.l: Letter from his cage to Bishop Theurel, January 3, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 186)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: When my head falls under the axe of the executioner, receive it, O loving Jesus! O Immaculate Mother! as the bunch of ripe grapes which falls under the scissors, as the full-blown rose which has been gathered in your honor.
q.l: Letter from his cage to Bishop Theurel, January 3, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 187)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: I have suffered nothing in comparison with my brethren. I have only to lay my head quietly on the block, under the axe of the executioner, and at once I shall find myself in the presence of Our Lord, saying, "Here am I, O Lord! Thy little martyr!"
q.l: Letter from his cage to Bishop Jeantet, January 20, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 189)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: A slight sabre-cut will separate my head from my body, like the spring flower which the Master of the Garden gathers for His pleasure. We are all flowers planted on this earth, which God plucks in His own good time, some a little sooner, some a little later. One is as the blushing rose, another the virginal lily, a third the humble violet.
q.l: Last letter to his father, from his cage, January 20, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 190)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: But before arriving at all this, the grain of wheat must be ground,—the bunch of grapes must be trodden in the wine-press. May I become only pure bread and wine, fit for the Master's use!
q.l: Last letter to his sister Mélanie, from his cage, January 20, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 192)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: My dearest Henry, you are now twenty-nine, the age of manhood. Be, then, a man. Do not waste your life in the frivolities of the world. To resist one's evil inclinations, to watch against the snare of the Evil One, and to practise one's religion—is to be really a man; not to do so, is to be less than a man.
q.l: Last letter to his brother Henry, from his cage, January 20, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 193)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: Guide your ship well. Let prudence take the helm, humility the rudder; let God be your compass, Mary your anchor of hope. And then, in spite of the disgust and bitterness which, like a howling sea, will sometimes overwhelm you, never be cast down.
q.l: Last letter to his brother Eusebius, from his cage, January 20, 1861 (ch. XIV, p. 195)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: The days of my pilgrimage lengthen strangely. The prefect is astonished that my sentence should be so long delayed. All the despatches from the king pass before my cage and each time one arrives I ask if my sentence of death is come. Each time the post-boy answers, 'No.' I hail every morning as the dawn of eternity, but evening comes, and I am still here.
q.l: Last message to Bishop Theurel, from his cage, February 1, 1861, the night before his execution (ch. XIV, p. 196)
q.tr: Lady Herbert, rev. James A. Walsh

q.t: Let us not worry about his last moments; Our Lord, the Blessed Virgin, his guardian angel, his holy patrons lavished on him more assiduous, loving care than a father, mother, brother or sister could have done. The providence of God is kind and admirable to His servants and infinitely more merciful than we can conceive.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to his father and mother on the death of his brother Louis on the way to China (Book I, ch. XIII, p. 90)

q.t: Alas! I have already lived more than thirty years which have passed like a dream and I have not yet learned how to live. When shall I learn how to die? Time disappears like a slight shadow; without our perceiving it, eternity arrives.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to his uncle on the death of his brother Louis (Book I, ch. XIII, p. 92)

q.t: That is all I wish. Since God has wished to die for us we must not fear to die for Him.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre
q.l: Reply to his uncle, who warned that nothing awaited him in China but martyrdom, as recorded by his biographer (Book I, ch. XIII, p. 94)

q.t: Ah! my dear uncle, my desires have to-day at last been granted. It was on the Feast of the Purification that permission was given me to go to China, which makes me think that in this matter, I owe much to the Blessed Virgin. Help me, please, to thank her and to beg her to thank Our Lord for me.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to his uncle on receiving leave to go to China, Paris, February 1835 (Book I, ch. XVI, p. 114)

q.t: During the first part of my voyage I had my soul in my hands; the fate of my brother Louis, the fears I felt, my inexperience of the sea, the weight of my infirmities left me but an uncertain prospect for the future. By the grace of God, I was never disconcerted. Does not the traveler, who, in the morning, finds himself enveloped in fog, continue the route, though he sees not its extent before him?
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to one of the Assistants of the Congregation, Macao, September 9, 1835 (Book II, ch. II, p. 135)

q.t: You know true happiness does not consist in having all kinds of consolations in this world, but in doing the will of God, in serving Him and in making as many serve Him as one can.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to one of his brothers, Macao, 1835 (Book II, ch. III, pp. 139-140)

q.t: I love the mysterious disposition of Providence which delights in having me live depending upon Him from day to day. When the time comes, we shall receive our mission. I shall not be troubled wherever they send me.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to one of the Assistants of the house at Paris, Macao, 1835 (Book II, ch. III, p. 146)

q.t: Reconcile yourself to God, from time to time, by a good confession. Do not imitate other young men who generally abandon the duties of their religion and behave badly. Do not be too much attached to the goods of this earth. Never forget that the affair of salvation is the business which should occupy you always and above all.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter to his brother (Book III, ch. III 'His Love of God', p. 274)

q.t: Cause me by Thy all powerful and infinite mercy, to be changed and transformed into Thee. May my hands be the hands of Jesus, may my eyes be the eyes of Jesus, may my tongue be the tongue of Jesus, may all my senses and my whole body serve but to glorify Thee, but especially transform my soul and all its powers; may my memory, my intellect, my heart be the memory, the intellect, the heart of Jesus
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre
q.l: Prayer he said daily before going up to the altar, as recorded by his biographer (Book III, ch. VI, p. 292; excerpt of a longer prayer)

q.t: The garden of Olives is not far from Calvary and if we do not take care we shall soon make Him die in our hearts.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre
q.l: Words on lukewarmness to a priest during Holy Week, as recorded by his biographer (Book III, ch. VII, p. 295)

q.t: This divine Master sees us, like His disciples, plunged in a shameful sleep; He comes to knock at the door of our souls to induce us to share His sorrows, but we deign not to pay attention to Him.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre
q.l: Reflections on Holy Week to the same priest, as recorded by his biographer (Book III, ch. VII, p. 296)

q.t: Do like those who are pressed by creditors and who have not wherewith to pay. They go and borrow it, do they not? Well, borrow, yourself, from the Blessed Virgin what you need. In her you will find faith, humility, love, in a word all that you lack; and with this you will have reason to be satisfied, for it will not be with your dispositions, but with those of Mary, that you will receive Jesus Christ.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre
q.l: Reply to a priest in spiritual dryness who meant to omit Mass, as recorded by his biographer (Book III, ch. VIII, p. 300)

q.t: After Mass by our actions we must testify that we have really received Jesus Christ, that we have been renewed and transformed in Him. Let us remember that Jesus Christ has immolated Himself for us, and let us often say: 'Jesus is immolated for me but on condition that I immolate myself for Him. My life must, then, be a continual immolation of myself to His holy will.'
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre
q.l: From the directions for offering Mass that he gave a priest who asked him for a method, as recorded by his…

q.t: No, I will be a no more marvellous man in China than in France; it is enough, my dear brother, if I may be a good little nag.
q.w: Life of Blessed John Gabriel Perboyre (letters)
q.l: Letter from China to his brother Jacques, who prayed that he might become a second St. Francis Xavier (Book III, ch. XIII, p. 351)

q.t: I am at my last hour; listen to me carefully. If I have had dealings with foreigners, it was for my religion, for my God; it is for him that I die. An immortal life is about to begin for me.
q.l: Spoken at his execution by the Han River, September 1846, as recorded by Bishop Ferréol; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 320
q.o: Je suis à ma dernière heure, écoutez-moi attentivement. Si j'ai communiqué avec les étrangers, c'est pour ma religion, c'est pour mon Dieu; c'est pour lui que je meurs. Une vie immortelle va commencer pour moi.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: We came into the world by a gift of God, and by another, still greater gift we have become, through our baptism, members of his Church: we bear a very precious name. But if we bear no fruit, what good will that name do us?
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 315
q.o: Venus au monde par un bienfait de Dieu, et par un autre bienfait plus grand encore, faisant, grâce à notre baptême, partie de son Église, nous avons un nom bien précieux; mais si nous ne portons pas de fruit, à quoi nous servira ce nom?
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Consider the farmer. At the proper season he plows his field and spreads manure on it, heeding neither cold nor heat nor his own toil. When he has sown good seed, if at harvest time the grain has come up well and ripened, he forgets all his sweat and his heart is full of joy.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 315
q.o: Considérez le cultivateur. Au temps convenable, il laboure son champ, y porte des engrais, et ne regarde ni au froid, ni à la chaleur, ni à sa peine. Après y avoir jeté de la bonne semence, si au temps de la moisson, le grain est bien venu et bien formé, il oublie toutes ses sueurs, et son cœur est plein de joie.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: The field of God is the earth, and men are the good seed. He enriches us with his graces, waters and nourishes us with the blood of his Son, who became man and died for us, and he teaches us by his holy Scriptures.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 316
q.o: le champ de Dieu, c'est la terre et les hommes sont les bonnes semences; il nous engraisse de ses grâces, nous arrose et nourrit du sang de son Fils incarné et mort pour nous, il nous instruit par ses saintes Écritures
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: My dearest brothers, know this well: our Lord Jesus, having come down into this world, himself suffered countless sorrows. By his sufferings he founded his Church, which must also grow amid crosses and tribulations. Since the Savior's ascension, from the apostles' time to this day, the Church has always grown amid a thousand persecutions; but whatever the world may do to attack and destroy her, it will never overcome her.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 316
q.o: Mes très-chers frères, sachez-le bien, N. S. Jésus, descendu en ce monde, a souffert lui-même des douleurs sans nombre. Par ses souffrances, il a établi son Église qui doit croître aussi au milieu des croix et des tribulations. Après l'ascension du Sauveur, depuis le temps des apôtres jusqu'à ce jour, l'Eglise a toujours grandi au milieu de mille persécutions; mais, quoi que le monde fasse pour l'attaquer et la détruire, il ne pourra la vaincre.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Yet it is written that God knows the number of our hairs, and that not one falls from our head without his permission. Let us therefore follow the holy will of the Lord and, taking the side of Jesus our leader, fight always against the world and the devil.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 316
q.o: Toutefois il est écrit que Dieu connaît le nombre de nos cheveux, et que pas un ne tombe de notre tête sans sa permission. Suivons donc la volonté sainte du Seigneur, et prenant le parti de notre chef Jésus, combattons toujours le monde et le démon.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: In this time of unrest and trouble, let us put on our armor like valiant soldiers and, as on a battlefield, fight and conquer. Above all, do not forget charity toward one another; help one another, and wait until God takes pity on you and grants your prayers.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 316
q.o: Dans ce temps d'agitation et de troubles, semblables à de vaillants soldats, revêtons nos armures, et comme sur un champ de bataille, combattons et soyons vainqueurs. Surtout n'oubliez pas la charité mutuelle, secourez-vous les uns les autres, et attendez que Dieu ait pitié de vous et exauce vos prières.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: The time of persecution is a trial from God; by victory over the world and the devil one gains virtue and merit. Do not let calamities frighten you, do not lose courage, and do not draw back in the service of God; rather, following in the footsteps of the saints, increase the glory of the Church and show yourselves true soldiers and subjects of the Lord.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 317
q.o: Le temps de persécution est une épreuve de Dieu; par la victoire sur le monde et le démon on acquiert la vertu et des mérites. Ne vous laissez pas effrayer par les calamités, ne perdez pas courage, et ne reculez pas dans le service de Dieu, mais plutôt, suivant les traces des saints, augmentez la gloire de l'Eglise et montrez-vous les vrais soldats et sujets du Seigneur.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Everything here below is ordained by God; everything that comes from him is reward or punishment. Persecution itself happens only by his permission; bear it patiently and for God, only beg him with tears to restore peace to his Church.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Postscript of the letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 317
q.o: Tout ici-bas est ordonné de Dieu, tout est de sa part récompense ou punition; la persécution elle-même n'arrive que par sa permission, supportez-la patiemment et pour Dieu; seulement, conjurez-le avec larmes de rendre la paix à son Eglise.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: My death will no doubt grieve you, and your souls will be in distress; but before long God will give you shepherds better than I am. So do not be too saddened, and strive with great charity to serve God as he deserves to be served.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Postscript of the letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 317
q.o: Ma mort vous sera sans doute sensible et vos âmes se trouveront dans la détresse; mais, sous peu, Dieu vous donnera des pasteurs meilleurs que je ne suis. Ne vous contristez donc pas trop, et efforcez-vous par une grande charité de servir Dieu comme il mérite d'être servi.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Let us remain united in charity, and after death we shall be united for eternity and shall enjoy God forever. I hope for this a thousand times, ten thousand times.
q.w: Last letter to the Christians of Korea
q.l: Postscript of the letter from prison, 1846; Dallet, vol. 2, p. 317
q.o: Restons unis dans la charité, et après la mort, nous serons unis pour l'éternité, et nous jouirons de Dieu à jamais. Je l'espère mille fois, dix mille fois.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Full of confidence in the Lord's mercy, we hope that he will give us the strength to confess his holy name until the last hour.
q.w: Letter from prison to Bishop Ferréol
q.l: Letter of 26 August 1846, original in Latin, French in Dallet, vol. 2, p. 314
q.o: Pleins de confiance en la miséricorde du Seigneur, nous espérons qu'il nous donnera la force de confesser son saint nom jusqu'à la dernière heure.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: I commend my mother Ursula to Your Lordship. After an absence of ten years she was granted to see her son again for a few days, and he is taken from her almost at once. Please, I beg you, console her in her grief.
q.w: Letter from prison to Bishop Ferréol
q.l: Letter of 26 August 1846, original in Latin, French in Dallet, vol. 2, p. 315
q.o: Je recommande à Votre Grandeur ma mère Ursule. Après une absence de dix ans, il lui a été donné de revoir son fils quelques jours, et il lui est enlevé presqu'aussitôt. Veuillez bien, je vous prie, la consoler dans sa douleur.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Surrounded by a rampart of snow, I waited for night, and to drive away the weariness that was coming over me, I said the rosary.
q.l: Letter from Seoul, 27 March 1845, on crossing the border into Korea (translated from the Latin); Dallet, vol. 2, p. 283
q.o: Entouré d'un rempart de neige, j'attendais la nuit, et pour chasser l'ennui qui me gagnait, je disais le chapelet.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Deprived of all human help, we put our only hope in God and in the Virgin Mary, said our prayers, and fell asleep.
q.l: Letter from Shanghai, 1845, on the storm at sea (translated from the Latin); Dallet, vol. 2, p. 286
q.o: privés de tout secours humain, nous mîmes notre seule espérance en Dieu et en la Vierge Marie, nous récitâmes nos prières, et nous nous endormîmes.
q.oe: Dallet, Histoire de l'Église de Corée, vol. 2 (1874)

q.t: Hear me, I implore you. I am not a stranger; nor have I come from the Philippine Islands. I am one of yourselves; a Japanese, and a member of the Society of Jesus.
q.w: Words from the cross at Nagasaki
q.l: Sermon from the cross, Nagasaki, 5 February 1597, as recorded by the eyewitnesses (Frois's relation); Boero, p. 153

q.t: I have been condemned to this cross, not for any crime, but solely because I have preached the law of our Lord Jesus Christ. And I esteem it a great happiness and honor to die for that law; and I thank the Lord for having thus crowned my labours.
q.w: Words from the cross at Nagasaki
q.l: Sermon from the cross, Nagasaki, 5 February 1597, as recorded by the eyewitnesses; Boero, p. 153

q.t: And, since that law commands us to pardon our enemies, and return good for evil, I pardon Taicosama and all those who have had a hand in my death.
q.w: Words from the cross at Nagasaki
q.l: Sermon from the cross, Nagasaki, 5 February 1597, as recorded by the eyewitnesses

q.t: Give to God these acts of humiliation which are ill-bestowed on me; and if you love me beseech Him to pardon me a sinner, for I am such.
q.w: Words at the place of martyrdom
q.l: To fellow Japanese who knelt to honor him on the hill of execution, Nagasaki, 5 February 1597, as recorded by the eyewitnesses

q.t: Implore Him to accept this miserable life of mine, which I willingly offer to Him on the cross as an atonement for my sins; and that it may be acceptable in His sight pray, I beseech you, that my cross and my death may be united to that of our Lord Jesus Christ.
q.w: Words at the place of martyrdom
q.l: Continuation of the same words on the hill of execution, as recorded by the eyewitnesses; Boero, p. 139

q.t: We are not criminals consigned to death for violation of the emperor's laws, and the only crime laid to our charge is, that we adore the one true God, creator of the universe, whom we love, and whose religion we preach. Taicosama, your emperor, knows not that religion; and he has, therefore, condemned us for announcing it.
q.w: Words on the road to Nagasaki
q.l: To the official guarding the prisoners at a village in Amakusa, January 1597, as recorded (the man was afterwards baptized)

q.t: We are sentenced to die on the cross. Let not your Paternity be troubled about us; for, through God's infinite goodness we find our consolation and joy in Him; and our only desire now is, that some day before arriving in Nangasasky (for when we reach that place it may be too late), one of the Fathers of the Society may come to hear our confessions.
q.w: Letter to the Vice-Provincial Pedro Gómez
q.l: Letter written on the way to Nagasaki, January 1597, and sent from Hakata; Boero, p. 109

q.t: Let him alone, he is acting as he ought.
q.l: Said to a Father who protested while an executioner pressed him down with his feet to bind him to the cross, as recorded by the eyewitnesses

q.t: To love Mary and to make her loved.
q.w: Motto written in his own blood
q.l: Written as a student at the seminary of Meximieux; Gilmore, p. 16

q.t: I thought what Christ wished that we should think when He said to His apostles: 'Whosoever heareth you, heareth Me.'
q.l: His reply, as a student, when asked what he thought of a sermon; Gilmore, p. 15

q.t: The devil was surely getting the best of me. A little more and he would have done me an ugly turn. Without understanding why, I was in an agony that bordered on despair. I owe it to the Blessed Virgin that I regained my courage.
q.l: Recalling, twenty years later, the day he nearly gave up his studies as a boy; Gilmore, p. 10

q.t: The more we study the human heart, the more deeply are we convinced that there are sparks of virtue in the most depraved souls; and that the most wicked would be judged with less rigor, if we kept in mind the strength of passion and the force of adverse circumstances.
q.l: A saying he often repeated as parish priest of Crozet; Gilmore, p. 35

q.t: But I am putting myself in God's hands and offering to Him the sacrifice of all that is pleasant. His will, not mine, be done!
q.l: Written from Crozet, on being proposed for a more attractive parish; Gilmore, p. 41

q.t: We must believe that He thinks of us and loves us; we ought to have our eyes fixed on him rather than on our faults. St. Francis de Sales tells us not to examine whether our hearts please Him, but whether His heart pleases us.
q.l: Counsel to his sister, Sister St. Dominic; Gilmore, p. 65

q.t: You would throw aside the sword of sacrifice before you have won the crown! Take courage, my child; try to strengthen yourself in your vocation; increase the number and the fervor of your prayers; throw yourself at the feet of the Blessed Virgin and beseech her to be your light and your strength in the way which will lead you to heaven. Remember, life is but a rapid passage across the plank which separates time from eternity.
q.l: Letter to his niece, a Visitation novice at Bourg who wished to go home; Gilmore, p. 65

q.t: All unworthy as I am of my sublime vocation I would not exchange it for a kingdom. I lack everything but good will. You will help me, I hope, to obtain the zeal and all the virtues necessary to the poorest of missionaries.
q.l: Letter from Le Havre before sailing for Oceania (1836)

q.t: We are all working for one reward, heaven. Let us waste no time on useless things; by doing so we expose ourselves to the danger of missing our end. Eternity will be quite long enough to rest us and repay us a hundredfold for the sufferings of this short life.
q.l: Letter from Futuna to his companion Brother Joseph Xavier; Gilmore, p. 147

q.t: Overcome with grief and weariness we sat on the sand at the foot of a cocoanut tree. I could still hear the wailing of those whose relatives had fallen, and I myself could only moan, praying to God for these people who have become my people, and whose salvation is entrusted to me. Oh, how long the tropical nights seem in times of sorrow!
q.l: Letter to Fr. Convers after tending the wounded of a battle on Futuna (1839); Gilmore, p. 151

q.t: It is true that in leaving France to come to Oceania I did not say good-bye to this vale of tears; but here, as in France, God knows His own and fills them with joy in the midst of suffering.
q.l: Letter from Futuna to Fr. Convers; Gilmore, p. 163

q.t: Pray, will you not, dear Father, that God's word may not be sterile in our mouths. Pray for all the natives of Oceania. The harvest is abundant, but the number of workers very small.
Ah God knows my heart! He knows how willingly I would brave the perils of the sea and the danger of persecution! But we are too few.
q.l: The same letter from Futuna; Gilmore, p. 164

q.t: This is the image of my God, Jesus Christ, Our Lord, who died for us on the cross.
q.l: His answer, holding up his crucifix, when a Futunian asked 'Isn't that your God?'; Gilmore, p. 171

q.t: The Faith has been planted in the island. It will lose nothing by my death because it is not the work of men, but of God.
q.l: Reply to a young man who feared he would be killed, a day or two before his martyrdom (April 1841); Gilmore, p. 182

q.t: You know, Lord, how much and how often on that very day you entrusted Germany to me, for which I was afterwards to go on caring, for which, like Father Faber, I was to give myself wholly, for which I longed to live and die.
q.w: Fragments of the Confessions and Testament
q.l: After receiving the papal blessing for his mission and praying at the tombs of the Apostles, Rome, September 1549
q.o: Nosti Domine quantopere et quoties illo ipso die mihi Germaniam commisisti, pro qua dein sollicitus esse pergerem, pro qua sicut Pater ille Faber me totum exhiberem, pro qua vivere morique cuperem.

q.t: At last, as though you had opened to me the heart of your most holy Body, which I seemed to see before my eyes, you bade me drink from that fountain.
q.w: Fragments of the Confessions and Testament
q.l: His prayer in St. Peter's before his solemn profession, 4 September 1549; Braunsberger I, p. 55
q.o: Tu tandem, velut aperto mihi corde sanctissimi Corporis tui, quod inspicere coram videbar, ex fonte illo ut biberem jussisti

q.t: And I longed above all that streams of faith, hope and charity might flow into me from it. I thirsted for poverty, chastity, obedience.
q.w: Fragments of the Confessions and Testament
q.l: Continuing the account of the same prayer, 4 September 1549; Braunsberger I, p. 55
q.o: Ego vero maxime cupiebam, ut fluenta fidei, spei, caritatis in me inde derivarentur. Sitiebam paupertatem, castitatem, obedientiam

q.t: Nor was the strength I felt after my profession a small thing: firmer hope, more perfect peace, greater circumspection, and a certain freer ability and grace in admonishing.
q.w: Fragments of the Confessions and Testament
q.l: On his solemn profession in the Society of Jesus, Rome, 1549; Braunsberger I, p. 57
q.o: Nec fuit exiguum, quod sensi, robur post Professionem. Spes firmior, pax integrior, circumspectio maior, et in admonendo liberior quaedam facultas et gratia.

q.t: But by your supreme charity I beg you, eternal God, to forgive both my parents every sin which your justice may perhaps still find in them and chastise.
q.o: Sed per summam te charitatem tuam aeterne DEVS oro, ut parenti utrique peccatum omne condones, quod in illis adhuc fortasse iustitia tua inuenit, atque castigat.

q.t: Truly, as a boy I thought many things, desired many things, said many things, did many things and left many things undone that did not become a Christian boy, and that very often deserved not only reproof but severe punishment.
q.l: Book I (c. 1570), on the faults of his childhood; Braunsberger I, p. 10
q.o: Vere multa puer cogitaui, multa concupiui, multa protuli, multa designaui, multa praetermisi, quae Christianum puerum dedecebant, neque tantum repraehensionem , sed seueram quoque castigationem persaepe merebantur.

q.t: Woe is me, how fruitlessly I spent hours, days, nights, weeks, months and years! How vain, needy and foolish I was, who ordered my life without fear and love of you, as if I did not know you as the author, guide and preserver of my life.
q.o: Hej mihj, quam infructuose horas, dies, noctes, hebdomadas, menses annosque consumpsi. Quam vanus, inops, stolidus fuj, qui sine timore et amore tuo vitam institui, uelut te vitae meae authorem, ducem et conseruatorem ignorarem.

q.t: For what can I offer you for those first years, which hold countless falls of that slippery age? What else can I offer you but that by which you are gladly appeased: the sacrifice of a contrite heart and a humbled spirit?
q.o: Quid enim possum pro primis illis annis, qui aetatis lubricae lapsus infinitos continent, quid possum aliud offerre tibi, nisi quo lubenter placaris, sacrificium contriti cordis, et spiritus humiliatj?

q.t: Therefore, while it is still the time for mercy, may your power conquer our frailty, your wisdom our ignorance, and your goodness overcome our malice.
q.l: Book I (c. 1570), praying for himself and the bad companions of his school years; Braunsberger I, p. 13
q.o: Ergo dum tempus est miserendi, vincat potentia tua, nostram fragilitatem, sapientia tua nostram ignorantiam, bonitas tua nostram malitiam superet

q.t: Glorious, rare, countless are your benefits, with which you have followed me from infancy through every age and in every place, so as to give me a happier opportunity than most others of living well and blessedly.
q.o: Praeclara sunt, rara sunt, infinita sunt beneficia tua, quibus inde ab infantia me per omnem aetatem, et ubique locorum es prosecutus, ut ad bene beateque vivendum occasionem feliciorem quam plerisque alijs mihi suppeditares.

q.t: He took on our humanity to heal my weakness, and to bestow on us his divinity and all his merits. May his death be my life; may his blood and wounds wash away my evils. As my flesh has often led me into sin, so may the flesh of so beloved and innocent a Son and Brother lead me back to pardon and turn you to mercy.
q.l: Book I (c. 1570), offering Christ to the Father; Braunsberger I, p. 28
q.o: Nostram ipse sumpsit humanitatem, meam ut sanaret infirmitatem, suamque divinitatem et merita omnia nobis largiretur. Illius mors mea vita sit: illius sanguis et vulnera diluant mala mea, sicut caro mea me crebro seduxit ad culpam , sic caro tam dilecti et insontis filij et fratris me reducat ad veniam, et te flectat ad misericordiam

q.t: Even if certain things present themselves to us, as we act, as good and fair at first sight, yet such is the weakness and inconstancy of the human mind that we often begin many things rashly, carry on coldly what we have begun, and do not bring it to a happy end.
q.l: Testament (c. 1596), part V; Braunsberger I, p. 51
q.o: Etsi uero quaedam prima fronte bona et speciosa sese nobis inter agendum offerunt, tamen ea humanae mentis est imbecilitas et inconstantia, ut multa saepenumero improuide inchoemus, inchoata uero frigide promoueamus, neque ad felicem terminum eadem perducamus.

q.t: Would that, just as your grace helped me in preaching the Gospel, so its fruit might also remain in others.
q.w: Fragments of the Confessions and Testament
q.l: On his preaching at Ingolstadt (from the Confessions, via Riess); Braunsberger I, p. 62
q.o: Utinam vero sicuti me tua juvit in Evangelizando gratia, sic etiam aliis fructus permaneat.

q.t: Would that your cross might have savor for me, King of eternal glory; would that the world, with its allurements and false colors, might lose its savor for me.
q.w: Fragments of the Confessions and Testament
q.l: Written of his time as vice-chancellor at Ingolstadt (from the Confessions, via Riess); Braunsberger I, p. 65
q.o: Utinam mihi sapiat crux tua, Rex aeternae gloriae, utinam desipiat mundus cum suis illecebris et fucis

q.t: I beg you, do not leave me this night, so that we may talk until morning about the joys of the heavenly life.
q.w: Dialogues of St. Gregory the Great, Book II (Life of St. Benedict)
q.l: Book II, ch. 33: her request to her brother Benedict at their last yearly meeting, as recorded by St. Gregory the Great
q.o: Quaeso te ne ista nocte me deseras, ut usque mane de coelestis vitae gaudiis loquamur.

q.t: See, I asked you, and you would not listen to me; I asked my Lord, and he heard me. So now, if you can, go out: leave me and go back to your monastery.
q.w: Dialogues of St. Gregory the Great, Book II (Life of St. Benedict)
q.l: Book II, ch. 33: her answer to Benedict after her prayer brought the storm, as recorded by St. Gregory the Great
q.o: Ecce te rogavi, et audiri me noluisti; rogavi Dominum meum, et audivit me. Modo ergo si potes, egredere, et me dimissa ad monasterium recede.

q.t: My Lord and my God, take from me everything that hinders me from coming to you! My Lord and my God, give me everything that brings me closer to you!
q.l: His daily prayer, first two petitions, by tradition his own and recorded from the 16th century
q.o: Mein Herr und mein Gott, nimm Alles von mir, was mich hindert zu Dir! Mein Herr und mein Gott, gib Alles mir, was mich fördert zu Dir!
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: My Lord and my God, take me from myself and give me to you!
q.l: His daily prayer, third petition; Ming, vol. 1, p. 241 (Ming adds in a note that some sources read 'gib mich ganz eigen Dir')
q.o: Mein Herr und mein Gott, nimm mich mir, und gib mich Dir!
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: Peace is always in God, for God is peace.
q.w: Letter to the Council of Bern
q.l: Letter dictated to the Mayor and Council of Bern, St. Barbara's day (4 December)
q.o: frid ist allwegen in got wan got der ist der frid
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: I thank you first and heartily for your kind gift, for by it I recognize your fatherly love, which gladdens me more than the gift.
q.w: Letter to the Council of Bern
q.o: ich dancken üch erstlich vnd fast üwer früntlichen gab wan ich erkennen dar dur üwer vätterliche liebe vnd die mich bas fröiwd den die gab
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: Therefore you should take care to build upon peace and to protect widows and orphans, as you have done until now; and whoever's good fortune increases on earth should be thankful to God for it.
q.w: Letter to the Council of Bern
q.o: Dar vmm so sönd jr lugen dz jr vff frid stellend witwen vnd weisen beschirment als jr dz noch vntzhar than heit vnd wesz glück sich vff dem ertrich meret Der sol got danckbar darum sin
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: If it does not weary you, I would also let you see my book, in which I learn and seek the art of this teaching.
q.w: Words recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.l: To a visiting pilgrim, showing him his meditation picture (the 'wheel'), as recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract (c. 1487; Dillingen print 1569)
q.o: wann dich nicht verdrießt, ſo wollt ich dich auch ſehen laſſen mein Buch, in welchem ich lerne und ſuch die Kunſt dieſer Lehr.
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: Do you see this figure? The divine Being is in the center, and that is the undivided Godhead, in which all the saints rejoice.
q.w: Words recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.l: Explaining his meditation picture to the pilgrim, as recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.o: Sieheſt du dieſe Figur? Alſo iſt das göttlich Weſen in dem Mittelpunkt, und das iſt die ungetheilte Gottheit, darinnen ſich alle Heiligen erfreuen.
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: The three points that go into the point of the inner circle are the three Persons; they go out from the one Godhead and have encompassed heaven and the whole world besides.
q.w: Words recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.l: Continuing the explanation of the picture, as recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.o: Die drei Spitz, die da gehen in den Punkt des inwendigen Zirkels, das ſind die drei Perſonen, und gehen aus von der einigen Gottheit, und haben umgriffen den Himmel, und darzu die ganze Welt
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)

q.t: And as they go out in divine power, so they also go back in, and they are one and undivided in eternal might; and that is what this figure means.
q.w: Words recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.l: End of the explanation of the picture (the three Persons), as recorded in the Pilgrim's Tract
q.o: Und als ſie ausgehen in göttlicher Gewalt, alſo gehen ſie auch ein, und ſind einig, und untheilig in ewiger Macht, und das bedeutet dieſe Figur.
q.oe: Ming, Der selige Bruder Nikolaus von Flüe (1861); Amiet (1843)
